On stage, two artists carefully manipulate, stack and balance a delicate landscape, risking collapse at any moment. The glass becomes partner, obstacle and quiet threat – demanding precision and trust between performers. Each action carries tension; each near-collapse asks what might happen next. Unexpected outcomes reveal a playful, precise exploration of our fragile world.
Venue description: Under its iconic towers on Nicolson Street, ZOO Southside hosts a carefully curated programme of stunning international contemporary performance. Bar open every night until 02:00 with free live events.
Venue accessibility: A number of shows will be offering BSL interpreted, audio described and captioned shows. Please see www.zoofestival.co.uk for up to date listings of these. Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Level access is via the rear entrance either from Quarry Close or off Nicolson St. between the venue and Dominos. Access to the Main House is across the stage via a small lift (80cm wide, 100cm deep)

Title: AFROBEAT PARTY: LONDON AFROBEAT COLLECTIVE | SAMSON SOUNDS | SAMEDIA SHEBEEN
Description:
Saturday 25 July, 8-10.30pmThe Queen's Hall

London Afrobeat Collective mix classic West African rhythms with jazz, funk and soul, and they do it with a powerful, dance-driven intensity. This is Afrobeat as it was meant to be heard - bold horn lines, propulsive percussion, deep bass and fearless improvisation, all driven by a collective spirit that turns every performance into a celebration. 

Rooted in the revolutionary sound of Fela Kuti but firmly grounded in the energy of modern London, the band create music that is both politically charged and joyfully danceable in their legendary live shows. They have rocked major stages around the world from Glastonbury Festival to the Shrine in Lagos, Nigeria – don't miss them when they come to Edinburgh! 

Joining them on the bill Glasgow afro and latin rhythm specialists Samson Sounds. Characterised by their uplifting stage presence, they blend elements of African highlife with dubstep, electronic beats and Jamaican reggae. The line-up is completed by renowned DJ Chris Knight from Samedia Shebeen. 

 Standing gigThis event is sold as standing as you are not allocated a seat. However, there are wooden pews downstairs and seats in the gallery which you can sit in should you prefer not to stand.

Title: ALI AFFLECK AND THE SWINGING CITY SIX
Description:
Vivacious vocalist Ali Affleck has a well deserved reputation for digging up some of the most exciting payers on the current vintage jazz scene and this year is no exception. She debuts a new band and a new repertoire celebrating the music of New Orleans, Chicago and Harlem. 

Torstein Kubban is a highly-acclaimed Norwegian jazz trumpeter known for his virtuosic command of early, classic, and Dixieland jazz. Critics and jazz reviewers consistently praise his blistering stage presence, technical precision, and phenomenal musicianship, often highlighting his "breathtaking attack”. Jonathan Greene is an in-demand clarinetist based in New Orleans, he is known by his peers and audiences alike for his lyrical phrasing and originality. Acclaimed British pianist Martin Litton graces the piano seat. A virtuoso player he effortlessly merges timeless melodies with dynamic improvisation. Guitarist Timmy Allen and bassist Roy Percy complete the all-star line up.

Title: NGUYÊN LÊ | CHRIS JENNINGS | ALYN COSKER TRIO
Description:
An exceptional meeting of three distinctive musical voices. Scottish drummer Alyn Cosker plays with explosive energy, precision and a master improviser’s touch. In this world premiere concert for EJBF he collaborates with two internationally-acclaimed musicians. Guitarist Nguyên Lê creates a richly-textured fusion of jazz, rock and Vietnamese musical traditions, delivered with dazzling technique and unmistakable lyricism. Completing the trio, Canadian bassist Chris Jennings is known for his supple tone, rhythmic assurance and instinctive musicality. Expect intricate melodic lines woven through driving grooves.

SUPPORTED BY THE SCOTTISH GOVERNMENT'S EXPO FUND

Title: THE BAD PLUS: THE FAREWELL TOUR
Description: Few bands have reshaped the sound and scope of modern jazz quite like The Bad Plus. From early reinterpretations of rock anthems to original compositions of striking complexity, their music is rhythmically daring, harmonically adventurous and driven by an almost telepathic interplay. Live, they are thrillingly direct. Founding members Reid Anderson (bass) and David King (drums) are joined by Ben Monder (guitar) and Chris Speed (tenor saxophone). This tour marks the closing chapter of their remarkable journey – don't miss your final chance to experience this unique band.

Title: TIMMY ALLAN SALUTES JIM HALL | MALCOLM MACFARLANE & ROSS MILLIGAN
Description: The guitar occupies an essential place in jazz being both a rhythm and melodic instrument. Timmy Allan recreates the music of one of the greats, Jim Hall. The American guitarist and composer was a masterful improviser with an unerring sense of melodic development, and the band will play his 1975 album Concierto as well as some surprises. In an opening set, the acoustic guitar duo of Malcolm MacFarlane and Ross Milligan play lush, textured compositions with extraordinary sensitivity.

Title: SOWETO KINCH
Description:
Closing out the festival, alto saxophonist, MC and composer Soweto Kinch has amassed an unprecedented array of accolades including two MOBO awards, two Urban Music Awards and a Mercury Prize nomination. A titan of the UK scene, his music is a thrilling mix of jazz and rap, with both tender and explosive moments. One of the most exciting and versatile musicians in British jazz.

Line up: Soweto Kinch (saxophone), Joshua Vadiveloo (bass), Louis Hamilton-Foad  (drums).

Title: KONRAD WISZNIEWSKI: THISTLE AND EAGLE
Description:
A festival commission from saxophonist Konrad Wiszniewski. This new music explores the shared links between Scotland and Poland over the recent centuries, inspired by the intertwining of their rich musical and cultural heritages. He will be joined by Tom Gibbs (piano), Brodie Jarvie (double bass) and Doug Hough (drums).

SUPPORTED BY THE SCOTTISH GOVERNMENT'S EXPO FUND

Title: SIMONA PARRINELLO QUARTET
Description:
Velvet voiced singer Simona Parrinello is inspired by Ellington and Strayhorn’s fusion of poetry and music. With her stellar Italian trio, she delivers a dynamic, haunting and evocative set.

SUPPORTED BY THE ITALIAN INSTITUTE OF CULTURE

Title: SONEDO
Description: This powerhouse live band forges a fresh blend of jazz, rap, and EDM, weaving a tapestry of jazz improvisation with sharp lyricism and modern grooves. Sonedo is the genre-bending project of Glasgow-based keyboardist Sean Edo Morrison.

Title: PETTER FROST FADNES | HAFTOR MEDBØE & SUE MCKENZIE
Description:
The acclaimed duo of Sue McKenzie (saxophones) and Haftor Medbøe (guitar and effects) deliver a suite of mesmerising improvisation, burning intensity and emotive depth. Opening the evening, Norwegian saxophonist Petter Frost Fadnes’ solo improvisation will be freshly baked and inspired by the ambience of the space.

PART OF SOUNDINGS: ADVENTURES IN IMPROVISED MUSIC, PRESENTED BY HAFTOR MEDBØE

Title: SULTAN STEVENSON
Description:
One of the most exciting emerging talents in contemporary jazz, pianist and composer Sultan Stevenson combines elegance, imagination and emotional depth. His influences include McCoy Tyner, Geri Allen and Herbie Hancock, and he draws on gospel, blues and contemporary jazz. With energising vamps and left-hand grooves that bring playful switches in intensity, his live performances are immersive and engaging.

"pianist’s modal voicings, syncopated single note lines and gospel shades spice the modern jazz mainstream with originality and flair." Financial Times

'ebulliently tasteful.. a sonic pleasure' UK jazz News

"His way of placing silences, and making a simple four-note lick grow into something significant, showed an incipient master at work." Telegraph

PART OF THE EDITION RECORDS SERIES

Title: PONGA
Description:
Tuesday 21 July, 6-7pmThe Jazz Bar

With Ponga, anything is possible. Formed in 2023, they thrive on the possibilities of free improvisation, which is at the core of everything they play. The Dutch trio switch between percussive, melodic, and harmonic roles, resulting in eclectic performances that encompass a variety of musical styles, including soundscapes, rock, jazz and classical music. Their performances blend compositional forms, infectious grooves, and unconventional melodies, often originating from experimentation and free play. With a shared background in theatre, expect both musical and theatrical fireworks from this exceptional band.

Remco Menting (drums/percussion), Timon Koomen (guitar), Yanna Pelser (viola/ vocals).

 PART OF SPARK: JAZZ FROM THE NETHERLANDS

Title: THE METZ FOUNDATION
Description:
Following an exciting debut in 2025, Luxembourg saxophonist Joël Metz returns to the festival with his own trio. Winner of the Luxembourg "Propulsion 2024" award, The Metz Foundation is an emerging jazz trio united by the shared vision of a raw, electric, and danceable sound. They seek to push sonic boundaries while fusing acoustic instruments and experimenting with sound design, improvisation, and unconventional sources of inspiration to enrich their musical language.

FUNDED BY KULTUR LUX

Title: SHIRT TAIL STOMPERS
Description:
Saturday 18 July, 6-7pmGeorge Square Spiegeltent

The Shirt Tail Stompers are steeped in the hot jazz and swing traditions of the 1920s and 30s, perfect for the surroundings of our traditional Spiegeltent. A young band with an old soul, they play this repertoire the way it’s meant to be heard - lively, rhythm-driven with tight ensemble playing.

Title: TENEMENT JAZZ BAND FOR KIDS
Description:
This one-hour show takes you on a fun adventure into the world of early jazz, designed especially for younger audiences. Diving into the heart of the band, you will experience the magic of live acoustic instruments.

Children must be accompanied by an adult.

Title: TRISKELION
Description: Blending jazz, electronica, soul and hip-hop, Triskelion are Mark Deering (synth and keyboard), George Chandler (bass), and Scott Jamieson (drums). Their original music showcases an exciting mix of unique textures and explosive grooves.

Title: MOOREN/WATSON/HERBERHOLZ/IRONS
Description:
Monday 20 July, 6-7pm The Jazz Bar

For this very special collaborative concert, rising star Dutch saxophonist Femke Mooren has been paired some of the leading lights of the next generation of Scottish jazz. She is a previous recipient of the Woman in Jazz Prize and winner of the 2023 Princess Christina Jazz Concours, and she joins Ali Watson, Simon Herberholz and Greg Irons for this one-off concert. Together, they promise evening of vibrant, cross-border musical collaboration that celebrates the boundless spirit of contemporary jazz. Bringing together distinct musical voices and shared creative curiosity, the project highlights the strength of international collaboration in shaping the next generation of jazz artists.

Femke Mooren (alto saxophone), Ali Watson (bass), Simon Herberholz (tenor saxophone), Greg Irons (drums).

 PART OF SPARK: JAZZ FROM THE NETHERLANDS | SUPPORTED BY THE SCOTTISH GOVERNMENT'S EXPO FUND

Title: BLUES AFTERNOON: TOBY MOTTERSHEAD BAND | JERRON PAXTON | TIM ELLIOTT & THE TROUBLEMAKERS
Description: The Troublemakers refresh some old school blues classics, showcasing Tim Elliott’s gravelly voice and trenchant harmonica. He is joined by guitarist Sandy Tweeddale and bass player Chris Agnew to deliver pre-war rural blues. Masterful multi-instrumentalist and deeply engaging storyteller, Jerron Paxton carries the torch for traditional acoustic blues and his solo performances are as entertaining as they are accomplished. Opening the afternoon, steel guitar player, singer, and raconteur, Toby Mottershead and his old time string band takes you on a tour of early blues and roots music from the 1920s onwards.

Title: JED POTTS & THE HILLMAN HUNTERS
Description:
The Hillman Hunters are a sensational trio, playing feel-good blues inspired by the great American sounds of the 50s and 60s, from Freddie King to Howlin’ Wolf. With infectious guitar riffs and deep grooves, their sound blends blues-infused rock with irresistible melodies, mixing classic influences with a growing catalogue of original songs. Led by guitarist and vocalist Jed Potts, the band deliver passionate blues with youthful energy and style, keeping the spirit of the blues alive.

Line up: Jed Potts (guitar), Jon Mackenzie (bass), Jonny Christie (drums).

Title: MALCOLM STRACHAN SEXTET
Description: Scottish trumpeter Malcolm Strachan is a composer and bandleader shaped by more than two decades at the heart of the UK jazz, funk and soul scene. His recent release, Look On The Bright Side, moves effortlessly between soul-jazz, Latin grooves and Afrobeat textures, all grounded in the rich, cinematic sound world of 1970s jazz. He leads a band brimming with talent with Mathew Kilner (saxophone), Paul Harrison (piano) and David Bowden (double bass) joining him for this performance.

Title: FERGUS McCREADIE MEETS WARREN VACHÉ
Description: For EJBF26, Fergus McCreadie presents a series of duo performances highlighting his interest in jazz from mainstream to contemporary. First up, he meets one of swing jazz’s giants, Warren Vaché. Known for his lyrical phrasing, Vaché brings a deep understanding of the tradition to the bandstand. Bringing together two world-class musicians from different generations, this meeting promises a dazzling interplay of ideas, where the richness of swing meets a fresh contemporary perspective.

Title: GAIA
Description:
If you caught her at last year’s festival, you’ll already know that singer GAÏA is one to watch. Born in France and now firmly rooted in Glasgow’s vibrant jazz scene, she has a sound that feels both intimate and assured. Blending jazz with contemporary R’n’B and neo-soul, there’s a natural fluidity to her phrasing and a songwriter’s instinct for melody. Her band is stacked with talent and features James Mackay (guitar) and Roan Anderson (drums).

SUPPORTED BY THE SCOTTISH GOVERNMENT'S EXPO FUND

Title: COLIN STEELE SEXTET
Description: Powerhouse Scottish trumpeter Colin Steele creates a celebration of melody and rhythm, infused with the energy, and improvisational flair of jazz. His Celtic-tinged themes come alive through a sextet of exceptional musicians: Konrad Wiszniewski and Michael Butcher (saxophones), Dave Milligan (piano) Mario Caribé (double bass), and Alyn Cosker (drums). Expect music that is exhilaratingly joyous - an enchanting journey where bold modern jazz meets traditional Scottish folk music.

Title: SYLVIE + URSULA
Description:
Bass player Ursula Harrison and vocalist and composer Sylvie Noble present an intimate acoustic conversation between the voice and double bass. They celebrate their shared love of both jazz and folk music, combining audacious improvisation and feminist tracts into a fresh and exhilarating mix.

PART OF SOUNDINGS: ADVENTURES IN IMPROVISED MUSIC, PRESENTED BY HAFTOR MEDBØE

Title: DICK LEE’S HOT CLUB HEPCATS
Description: Making their festival debut, this Hot Club inspired quintet play swing jazz classics from the likes of Benny Goodman, Django Reinhardt and Duke Ellington. This inter-generational band is led by clarinettist Dick Lee and features the dynamic guitars of Ronan Toal and Iain McNally, Martin Foster (reeds) and Steven Jack (double bass).

Title: MONNEAU | KILNER | STEPEHN | COSKER
Description:
Belgian bassist Jim Monneau joins a Scottish trio of Matthew Kilner (saxophone), Graeme Stephen (guitar) and Alyn Cosker (drums). They will exchange compositions and inspiration in a first meeting that promises spontaneity and the thrill of musical chemistry.

SUPPORTED BY THE SCOTTISH GOVERNMENT'S EXPO FUND

Title: MICHELLE WILLIS
Description: Captivating, charismatic and mesmerising, Canadian singer Michelle Willis channels Joni Mitchell with her sparkling vocals, mean piano playing and fantastic songwriting skills. She was mentored by the late David Crosby and toured with his Lighthouse band. He described her as: "Fluid, powerful, graceful... such a fine writer... a soulful, rich, deep player and bandleader who just swings as if her life depended on it. One of the best singers I’ve ever heard in my life. Of all. Ever.” If you love Joni, Carole King or Bob Dylan - this one's for you.

Title: JIM MULLEN: BURNS
Description:
Celebrating his 70th year, Jim Mullen is arguably the finest jazz guitarist the UK has produced, and he gets into a groove with his take on the songs of Robert Burns. From Banks and Braes to My Love Is Like A Red, Red Rose, expect hard swinging, melodic, blues-drenched modern jazz, and plenty of musical fireworks as he is joined by David Milligan (piano), Mario Caribé (bass) and Alyn Cosker (drums).

“mellow, soulful guitar and legendary fluency” (Observer)

Title: THE CINELLI BROTHERS WITH SPECIAL GUEST ALICE ARMSTRONG
Description: London’s dynamic four-piece, The Cinelli Brothers, deliver a gutsy fusion of southern soul, Chicago blues-funk, and classic electric blues. Steeped in the sounds of Chess to Stax and Motown - the band delivers original music that honour these traditions while injecting a contemporary spark. For EJBF26 they present a special show as they are joined by multi award-winning singer Alice Armstrong.

Title: NORMAN&CORRIE
Description:
The band of the moment. The duo of saxophonist Norman Willmore and drummer Corrie Dick have been setting the jazz world alight. With their unique blend of Shetland folk music meeting the urgency of contemporary jazz, they conjure a sound both ancient and startlingly new. Their festival commission offers a glimpse of the next chapter of their compelling story.

SUPPORTED BY THE SCOTTISH GOVERNMENT'S EXPO FUND

Title: FERGUS McCREADIE MEETS MATHIAS EICK
Description: Scottish piano sensation Fergus McCreadie collaborates with some of his musical heroes at this year’s festival. For the second concert in the series, he is joined by trumpeter Mathias Eick. A key feature on the Norwegian jazz scene, Eick’s haunting and elegiac tone has graced many ECM albums, highlighting his cinematic interest in musical storytelling.

Title: MORTEN GUNNAR LARSEN
Description: The current king of ragtime piano, Norwegian Morten Gunnar Larsen spans the rollicking rags of Jelly Roll Morton and the playful stride of Eubie Blake to the daring flair of Jabbo Smith. Steeped in tradition yet alive with excitement, his performances are a thrilling celebration of jazz history. Larsen’s solo set channels the spirit of New Orleans and Tin Pan Alley.

Title: EJBF COMMUNITY BAND
Description: Our very own EJBF Community Band presents a special concert performing a selection of jazz standards alongside tunes from jazz legends Benny Golson and Roy Hargrove, with a few hits from the Average White Band and the Blues Brothers thrown in for good measure! There will be something for everyone with this great afternoon of music.

Title: TAO
Description:
Saturday 18 July, 6-7pmThe Jazz Bar

Led by drummer Roan Anderson (winner of BBC Young Scottish Jazz Musician 2025), TAO returns with a festival commission. Drawing on jazz, electronic and ambient influences, they create music that is immersive and expansive.

SUPPORTED BY THE SCOTTISH GOVERNMENT'S EXPO FUND

Title: RIGID SOUL
Description:
Rigid Soul are an eclectic, high-energy band rooted in blues and swaggering 60s rock. Their sound is stretching into jazz grooves and swirling psychedelic colours. Expect punchy riffs and infectious rhythms.

Line up: Kyle Hood (guitar/vocals), Rachel Duns (sax/organ/vocals), Rory Buchanan (bass/vocals), Lewis Ross (drums).

Title: JERRON PAXTON
Description:
Friday 24 July, 7.30-9.30pmThe Queen's Hall

A masterful multi-instrumentalist and a deeply engaging storyteller, Jerron Paxton carries the torch for traditional acoustic blues. He moves effortlessly between blues, folk, ragtime and early jazz, bringing each tradition vividly to life. His musicianship is authoritative yet completely unshowy, driven by an infectious sense of joy and an intuitive understanding of the music’s roots. 

Paxton’s solo performances are as entertaining as they are accomplished. His easy humour, rich singing voice and natural rapport with an audience create concerts that feel intimate and generous, even in large rooms. He doesn’t just play music, he invites listeners into it, sharing its history, humanity and enduring relevance. 

Soulful and irresistibly engaging, this American bluesman delivers concerts that stay with you long after the final note. A must-see performance from a true audience favourite. 

Jerron Paxton will also play St Andrew Square Spiegeltent as part of the Blues Afternoon on Sunday 26 July. Tickets will go on sale for this show on Thursday 30 April 2026.

 Tickets purchased via EJBF are inclusive of all fees. Tickets purchased via The Queen's Hall are subject to a £1.50 booking fee.

Title: IMMANUEL WILKINS QUARTET
Description:
Tuesday 21 July, 9-10.30pmGeorge Square Spiegeltent

Destined for the jazz hall of fame, American saxophonist and Blue Note recording artist Immanuel Wilkins is one of the most exciting musicians working in the genre today. Dynamic and pioneering, he has already earned a reputation for fearless creativity and emotional depth, blending avant-swing with soulful, church-rooted melodies. With his quartet, he has graced some of the most esteemed stages and jazz festivals in the world. Witness the arrival of one of the defining voices of the next generation in modern jazz - perfect for fans of of Kamasi Washington, Miles Davis and Shabaka Hutchings.

“A lustrous talent” The Guardian

“brimming with fresh harmonic ideas, but also an emotional potency that resonates long afterwards” Mojo

“abundant creativity, firepower, and riveting group communication" All Music

Line up: Immanuel Wilkins (saxophone), Micah Thomas (piano), Ryoma Takenaga (bass), Kayvon Gordon (drums).

Title: BRIAN KELLOCK: A LIFE IN MUSIC
Description:
Thursday 23 July, 7.30-9.30pmThe Queen's Hall

A towering figure on the UK jazz scene and a cherished presence at the festival, Brian Kellock’s warmth, humour and musicianship left a mark on everyone who played with him, and everyone who heard him.  

This all-star, one-of-a-kind concert features special guests travelling from across the world to pay homage. An incomparable front line of Liane Carroll (vocals), Scott Hamilton and Alan Barnes (saxophones), Warren Vaché (trumpet), meets a stellar rhythm section David Newton (piano and musical director), Dave Green (bass) and Max Popp (drums). Kenny Ellis (bass) and Fergus McCreadie (piano) also make special guest appearances.

Expect an evening of world-class music, full of the tunes that Brian loved, packed with generosity, humour and wonderful storytelling, as we pay tribute to the musical genius and virtuosity of Brian Kellock.

Title: BLUES AFTERNOON: LOUIS CROSSLAND | ANDREW ROBERT EUSTACE BAND | JENSEN INTERCEPTORS EXPANDED
Description:
Louis Crossland | Andrew Robert Eustace Band | Jensen Interceptors Expanded

 Sunday 19 July, 1-4pmGeorge Square Spiegeltent

A homage to the blues guitar. Jensen Interceptors are a band who deliver rocking blues straight out of the Chicago tradition. Fronted by Gary Martin’s vocals and harmonica, John Bruce is joined by three other guitarists including Al Brown in this specially expanded line-up. Guitarist Andrew Eustace has the blues in his bones. With gritty vocals and driving guitar riffs, he skilfully evokes the greats of years gone by. Louis Crossland makes his festival debut, opening the afternoon with his blend of blues, soul, country, and R’n’B.

Title: KEARNEY | POTTS | SMIT
Description: Stroll down Frenchmen Street with Nicole Smit, Jed Potts and Mike Kearney. Three stellar, genre crossing musicians celebrate the music of New Orleans in a stripped back show. From the sultry vocals of Nicole Smit, through the stride piano of Mike Kearney to laid back R’n’B from guitarist Jed Potts, this is music delivered from the heart, embracing excitement, sadness, and technical prowess.

Title: DAVINA & THE VAGABONDS
Description:
Saturday 18 July, 7.30-9.30pmThe Queen's Hall

Davina & The Vagabonds are one of those rare bands that audiences fall in love with. A long-standing festival favourite, each visit feels more electric than the last, so it’s no surprise their shows so often sell out.  

Davina has been compared to the likes of Etta James, Janis Joplin and Billie Holiday, but she’s truly one-of-a-kind. She commands the stage from the first note, drawing audiences in with her powerhouse voice, wicked humour and total emotional honesty. One moment she’s belting out roof-raising blues, the next she’s breaking hearts with a ballad.  

Backed by a tight band that play jazz, blues, soul, swing and rock ‘n roll with flair, precision and joy, Davina delivers an evening packed with fearless charisma, razor-sharp musicianship and a huge sense of fun. 

Davina & The Vagabonds will also play George Square Spiegeltent on Sunday 19 and Monday 20 July 2026. Tickets will go on sale for these two shows on Thursday 30 April 2026.

Title: THE PITT
Description:
After last year’s sellout success, we return to The Pitt, bringing the hottest sounds to this iconic venue down by the water’s edge. With a dancefloor filling mix of funk, hip-hop and more, we're showcasing three Scottish bands at the cutting edge.

A dynamic sextet, Harry Weir’s Blue Boar Brass are a contemporary jazz and hip-hop outfit who play with huge drive and attack. Harry’s trenchant sax sits on top of a band weaving together a scorching mix of pulsating grooves.

Brimming with energy and drive, Mama Terra is the Scottish jazz and soul sensation led by pianist Marco Cafolla and Konrad Wiszenewski. With influences including John and Alice Coltrane, Miles Davis and Kamasi Washington, they blend soulful grooves, driving bebop, and rich spiritual jazz influences.

Fresh from winning the 2025 Scottish Album of the Year award, Kai Reesu is a band on the rise. Blending elements of jazz, hip-hop, psychedelia and grime, the Glasgow band are inspired by hip-hop beatmaking, and the greats of 70s jazz fusion and feature vocals from Scotland-based LA rapper Jurnalist.

Title: HARMEN FRAANJE
Description:
Saturday 18 July, 2.30-3.30pm St Mark's Episcopal Church, Portobello

Heralded by All About Jazz as one of the most impressive European pianists of the past decade, Harmen Fraanje is a Dutch jazz musician and composer with a unique voice in contemporary improvisational music. Thanks to his collaborations with leading musicians such as Ambrose Akinmusire, Mark Turner, Arve Henriksen, Trygve Seim and Han Bennink, he has now become a major figure on the European jazz scene. His music breathes lyricism and introspection, with a refined balance between minimalism and expressive depth creating soundscapes of delicate beauty. In his playing, jazz, classical harmony, and world music blend organically, making the beautiful surroundings of St Mark's Church the perfect setting for this solo concert.



 PART OF SPARK: JAZZ FROM THE NETHERLANDS

Title: TENEMENT JAZZ BAND
Description:
Kicking off the 2026 festival, Tenement Jazz Band are Edinburgh's finest young purveyors of early jazz. Known for their infectious energy and authentic New Orleans sound, they breathe new life into the joyful, foot-tapping sounds of the 1920s and 30s in the company of their special guest drummer Nicholas D. Ball. With Nick driving the band, this concert promises to be an inspiring journey through the red-hot roots of jazz, with scorching renditions of early recordings and fresh takes on some lesser-known tunes.

 Line up: Charles Dearness (trumpet), John Youngs (vocals/banjo), Paddy Darley (trombone), Rory Clark (sousaphone), Stephen Feast (clarinet), Nicholas D. Ball (drums).

Title: FERGUS McCREADIE MEETS XHOSA COLE
Description: For the third concert in his EJBF26 series, Fergus McCreadie is joined by acclaimed British saxophonist Xhosa Cole. A former BBC Young Jazz Musician of the Year, Cole is celebrated for his expressive playing and deep connection to the lineage of jazz, drawing inspiration from masters such as Thelonious Monk while forging a voice that is unmistakably his own. Rooted in tradition yet alive with curiosity and invention, this duo promises an intimate and spirited musical conversation, full of spontaneity, lyricism and shared imagination.

Title: THE VIPER CLUB
Description:
Gyspy jazz violin superstar Tcha Limberger joins forces with the exhilarating Armstrong inspired trumpeter Jérôme Etcheberry for compelling and hard-swinging jazz from 1930’s New York. Together with the impeccable Dave Kelbie on guitar, and Sebastien Girardot on bass, they celebrate pre-eminent jazz violinist Stuff Smith, who in New York in the 30s, worked alongside Jelly Roll Morton, Louis Armstrong and Ella Fitzgerald.

“A collective résumé which reads just like a who’s who of early jazz” Just Jazz UK

Title: JAMES BROWN IS ANNIE PLAY BOTTOM DOLLAR
Description: Be the first to hear the next chapter from Edinburgh groove merchants James Brown is Annie as they present their new album Bottom Dollar. Drawing inspiration from the soul-funk of Average White Band, they blend tight horn lines, deep-pocket rhythms and sharp musicianship into a high-energy set that moves effortlessly between funk, soul and jazz. Expect punchy arrangements and serious grooves.

Title: BRIAN MOLLEY QUARTET PLAY SAXOPHONE COLOSSUS
Description:
Saturday 18 July, 9-10.30pmSt Bride’s Centre

Recorded in 1956 and still electrifying seventy years on, Saxophone Colossus is the record that confirmed Sonny Rollins as a towering creative force. Brian Molley Quartet pay tribute to the album, alongside Rollins’ favourites from legendary 1950s albums Way Out West and Newk's Time.

Title: LIAM O'NEIL QUINTET
Description: Trumpeter Liam O’Neil pushes the boundaries between contemporary classical, modern jazz, and electronic music with driving uncompromising rhythms. His stellar band features vocals from Laura Osa and Paul Harrison on piano.

Title: HARBEN KAY QUARTET | CHRIS AMER SEXTET
Description:
A double bill featuring two of the most exciting and individualistic voices in Scottish jazz.

Saxophonist Harben Kay creates thoughtful compositions that are emotionally resonant. With their long-term band, they create a sound that is both globally influenced and unmistakably their own. Their intelligent writing is both intensely personal and thoughtful and is beautifully complemented by their liquid tenor tone and the empathy they share with their band of Peter Johnstone (piano), Calum Gourlay (bass), and Alyn Cosker (drums). Their assured performances merge contemporary ideas  with conventional jazz virtues creating a sound that is both globally influenced, with Scottish inflections and unmistakably their own.

Opening the concert, guitarist Chris Amer’s music is strongly melodic, with elegant improvisations and chorale-like orchestrations. He treads his own path influenced by poets like Norman MacCaig, the Scottish landscape, and straddling the ever-blurring boundary between jazz and traditional Scottish music. For his EJBF debut he is joined by Ali Watson (bass), Fergus McCreadie (piano), Matt Carmichael(saxophone) and Stephen Henderson (drums)."There's a beguiling flow to Amer's music, the bright strings of tenor guitar laced with licks and murmurs of round-toned electric, that defies pigeonholing.” The Scotsman

Title: BLUES AFTERNOON: SANDY TWEEDDALE & GUS MUNRO | GERRY JABLONSKI BAND | TRUE STRAYS
Description: True Strays blend alt-Americana with blues rock anthems filled with soul and grit. They are exhilarating live, with a powerful fusion of towering choruses and thunderous riffs, all drenched in soul. Gerry Jablonski Band turn the volume up loud! They deliver propulsive, high-energy shows wrapped in blues power. The afternoon opens with a set from two talented Scottish blues guitarists, Sandy Tweeddale and Gus Munro. Their band are inspired by the sophisticated slidestyles of Derek Trucks and the Allman Brothers.

Title: MARIANNE MCGREGOR SEXTET
Description:
Multi award-winning Scottish vocalist Marianne McGregor fronts a new sextet as she delivers an afternoon of captivating vocals, sparkling musicianship and songs delivered with flair. With the tone of Amy Winehouse, an Ella-like improvisational freedom and the ability to capture emotion like Billie Holiday, she is joined by a top band of Scottish musicians.

Line up: Marianne McGregor (vocals), Brian Molley (saxophone/flute), Paul Harrison (piano), Samuel Parkinson (guitar), Mario Caribé (double bass), Max Popp (drums).

Title: SHIRT TAIL STOMPERS
Description:
A must for swing dancers. The Shirt Tail Stompers are steeped in the hot jazz and swing dance traditions of the 1920s and 30s, delivering the music with an infectious joy. A young band with an old soul, they play this repertoire the way it’s meant to be heard - lively, rhythm-driven with tight ensemble playing. It’s music that's impossible to sit still for – bring your dancing shoes!

PRESENTED IN ASSOCIATION WITH EDINBURGH JAZZ & JIVE CLUB

Title: LAURA OSA QUARTET
Description:
Scottish rising star singer Laura Osa’s sweet and ethereal vocals blend seamlessly with her powerful songwriting. Recognised for her ability to infuse emotion into every note, her music offers a stunning fusion of R’n’B, gospel, and jazz.

You may have seen her performing with the Scottish National Jazz Orchestra, or with Laura Macdonald - experience her exciting new quartet as they make their EJBF debut.

Title: EDINBURGH SCHOOLS JAZZ ORCHESTRA
Description:
Saturday 25 July, 11.30am-12.30pmSt Bride's Centre

Enjoy the glory of the full big band experience with Edinburgh's own top youth jazz band. Under the direction of Kelan Rooney, the band is packed with some exceptional talent – expect big band classics and a few surprises.

Title: ELEANOR COLEE QUARTET
Description: Glasgow-based saxophonist and composer Eleanor Colee is a rising star on the Scottish jazz scene. Blending contemporary and spiritual jazz with folk inspired elements, she takes inspiration from Pharoah Sanders and Nubya Garcia.

Title: MARTIN HARLEY SOLO
Description: Master slide guitarist Martin Harley captivates with an up close and personal solo set. Blending delta blues with rich acoustic folk, his heartfelt music continues to push boundaries.

Title: MATT CARMICHAEL SEXTET
Description:
Saturday 18 July, 8.30-10.30pmGeorge Square Spiegeltent

Scottish saxophonist Matt Carmichael is one of the most distinctive voices on the UK jazz scene, with his deeply emotive fusion of lyrical jazz and evocative folk influences. Drawing on the traditional music he grew up with, while echoing the harmonic sophistication of Brad Mehldau and the cinematic intimacy of Bon Iver, his compositions feel both rooted and resolutely contemporary. Performed by an exceptional all-star sextet made up of Scottish and Norwegian artists, including Kjetil Mulelid on piano, the music unfolds with a rare collective chemistry. 

"From the get-go it's hard not to be charmed by Matt Carmichael's breathy melodicism, unabashedly steeped in his Scottish heritage." Jazzwise

Line up: Matt Carmichael (saxophone), Sarah-Jane Summers (violin), Chris Amer (guitar), Kjetil Mulelid (piano), Ali Watson (bass), Per Oddvar Johansen (drums).

 SUPPORTED BY THE SCOTTISH GOVERNMENT'S EXPO FUND

Title: EVAN AND CAROLINA'S SUPER DUPER GROUP & FUN
Description:
Friday 17 July, 6-7pmThe Jazz Bar

Known for her authentic and emotionally charged voice, Carolina Gemmell is a versatile vocalist, active in the Amsterdam jazz and soul scene, and pianist Evan van der Feen has received multiple awards for his expressive and dynamic playing. Together, they form a musical partnership in which improvisation is central. Evan and Carolina's Super Duper Group & Fun performs both original repertoire and jazz standards with a playful, open spirit creating a world that is dreamy and inventive. The balance between her voice and his piano playing creates introspective moments that alternate with playful grooves, making each performance feel like a unique, intimate experience. 

Carolina Gemmell (vocals), Evan van der Feen (piano), David Guerreiro (double bass), Ludvig Søndergaard (drums).

PART OF SPARK: JAZZ FROM THE NETHERLANDS

Title: NABOU
Description:
Belgian trombonist Nabou Claerhout is one of the most distinctive new voices on the European jazz scene. Her debut record with Edition Records, Indigo, has a warm, expressive tone and a fearless sense of adventure, blending playful lyrical melodies with bold, contemporary grooves. Her quartet's interplay is tight, responsive and full of spark, moving effortlessly between moments of quiet reflection and surging energy. Expect imaginative compositions, rich textures and a sound that is fresh, confident and quietly captivating.

"In her striking album Indigo, trombonist Nabou Claerhout reaches a decisive new stage in her artistic journey." All Music

Nabou Claerhout (trombone), Trui Amerlinck (double bass), Gijs Idema (electric guitar), Daniel Jonkers (drums)

PART OF THE EDITION RECORDS SERIES | FUNDED BY FLANDERS

Title: TUBA SKINNY
Description:
Friday 17 July, 7.30-9.30pmThe Queen's Hall

Making their Edinburgh debut, Tuba Skinny are a powerhouse ensemble channelling the spirit of early New Orleans jazz.  

Young, virtuosic and unmistakably the real deal, their sound is rooted in early jazz, blues and ragtime, bringing history to life with soulful vocals, rich horn harmonies, and driving rhythms. Their sound is joyful and infectious, and, while it's evident the band treasures the sense of history evoked by these vintage tunes, the players' natural exuberance makes the music feel irresistibly alive. 

Don't miss this rare opportunity to experience a true New Orleans street band in full flow.

Title: LOUIS AND THE DIVAS
Description:
Celebrated New Orleans singer Tricia Boutté joins Dave Batchelor’s all-star band, featuring trumpeter Colin Steele. Together, they celebrate the music Louis Armstrong made with singers in his long career. From Ma Rainey to Ella Fitzgerald via Bessie Smith and Billie Holliday, this will be an afternoon full of wonderful music, great singing and fabulous playing.

Line up: Tricia Boutté (vocals), Colin Steele (trumpet), Dave Batchelor (trombone/vocals), Campbell Normand (piano), Andy Mitchell (bass), Alastair Morrow (drums).

Title: D.K. HARRELL
Description:
One of the leading voices of the new generation of blues players, D.K. plays with honesty, authority and heart. His music nods to the greats, with a sound that is steeped in tradition yet thrillingly alive in the present. The Louisianan bluesman combines soulful storytelling with an easy, magnetic presence. He knows how to draw an audience in and keep them there, so it's easy to see why he’s a major draw at blues festivals around the world.

“D.K. Harrell picks up the baton and carries his [music] into the future, creating formidable electric blues.” Vintage Guitar

Title: BLUE GIANT ORKESTAR
Description: Blue Giant Orkestar are an irrepressible Balkan-Celtic fusion octet - a riotous melting pot of blazing brass, searing fiddle, thunderous tuba, one enormous Russian concert accordion and a percussion section that hits with joyous, floor-shaking force. Drawing inspiration from Balkan horos, Serbian brass festivals, Turkish pop, Bulgarian accordion fireworks and even a dash of Scottish ceilidh, their music is bold, high-octane and utterly infectious. Expect driving rhythms, dazzling musicianship and a party atmosphere.

Title: DAVINA & THE VAGABONDS
Description: Davina and The Vagabonds are a long-standing festival favourite. Davina has been compared to the likes of Etta James, Janis Joplin and Billie Holiday, but she’s truly one-of-a-kind. She commands the stage from the first note, drawing audiences in with her powerhouse voice, wicked humour and total emotional honesty. Backed by a tight band that play jazz, blues, soul, swing and rock ‘n roll with flair, precision and joy, Davina delivers an evening packed with fearless charisma.

Title: TENEMENT JAZZ BAND FOR KIDS
Description:
This one-hour show takes you on a fun adventure into the world of early jazz, designed especially for younger audiences. Diving into the heart of the band, you will experience the magic of live acoustic instruments.

Children must be accompanied by an adult.

Title: BLUE MILK
Description: One of Scotland’s finest blues outfits, Blue Milk are influenced by turn-of-the-century Delta blues and electric 60s and 70s blues rock. With a raw energy, their exhilarating live performances are a powerhouse of grit and groove.

Title: VAN RULLER // HOGENHUIS
Description:
Saturday 18 July, 6-7.30pmSt Bride's Centre

In this very special concert, guitarist and Dutch jazz legend Jesse van Ruller (who has performed with the likes of Pat Metheny, Mike Stern, Christian McBride and Peter Bernstein) pairs with rising star saxophonist Maarten Hogenhuis. Even though their musicianship is rooted in jazz, they’re also inspired by singular bands and songwriters such as Sufjan Stevens, Andrew Bird, Grizzly Bear and Blake Mills. With two albums under their belt, this duo deliver a compelling musical dialogue, where warm guitar lines and expressive saxophone meet in lyrical, free-flowing improvisation. They present a beautifully understated dialogue between guitar and saxophone, balancing melodic elegance with adventurous improvisation. 

Jesse van Ruller (guitar), Maarten Hogenhuis (alto saxophone).

 PART OF SPARK: JAZZ FROM THE NETHERLANDS

Title: BLUES AFTERNOON: AL BROWN & THE BLUELIGHTERS | THE ZAC SCHULZE GANG | MARTIN HARLEY TRIO
Description:
Slide guitar master, Martin Harley, blends delta blues and rich acoustic folk, with a snarling rock ‘n roll edge. For three decades, he’s captivated audiences, playing at prestigious venues and festivals like Glastonbury and the Royal Albert Hall. Opening the afternoon, guitarist Al Brown brings his trademark deeply tasteful and expressive playing to front the Bluelighters, widely known for delivering powerhouse performances with musical depth.

Unfortunately, Zac Schulze has had a fall and damaged his hand (we wish him a speedy recovery). Jesse Garwood, the 18 year old blues guitar sensation will replace him in the programme. His trio will play hard hitting originals and dynamic covers with a raw and essential energy.

Title: MODERN VIKINGS | ALI WATSON QUARTET
Description:
Modern Vikings brings together some of Scotland’s most distinctive jazz voices under the leadership of drummer Stephen Henderson. Together, they forge a high-energy sound rooted in jazz improvisation and inspired by the rich melodic traditions of Scottish and Scandinavian folk music. Henderson is joined by Konrad Wiszniewski (saxophone), Fergus McCreadie (piano), Graeme Stephen (guitar) and David Bowden (double bass).Bass player Ali Watson is joined by Matt Carmichael (saxophone), Fergus McCreadie (piano) and Greg Irons (drums). They draw on the traditions of Scottish folk, alongside impressionist classical music, creating music that feels expansive, evocative and quietly captivating.

 SUPPORTED BY THE SCOTTISH GOVERNMENT'S EXPO FUND

Title: JOOLS HOLLAND
Description:
JOOLS HOLLANDand his Rhythm & Blues Orchestrawith special guest star ROACHFORDand guest vocalists RUBY TURNERLOUISE MARSHALL & SUMUDU JAYATILAKA+ support from Freddie Lennox

Join us for an unforgettable night of world-class music as Jools Holland and his renowned Rhythm & Blues Orchestra take over Usher Hall for the Edinburgh Jazz & Blues Festival! Bursting with electrifying energy, irresistible grooves, and Jools’ signature boogie-woogie brilliance, the 20-piece band brings together exceptional musicianship and joyful, feel-good entertainment. Featuring guest vocalists Ruby Turner, Louise Marshall and Sumudu Jayatilaka, the line-up is completed by rock and soul sensation, Roachford.

With support from Freddie Lennox, a songwriter inspired by Jackson Browne, Mississippi John Hurt, Bob Dylan, Muddy Waters, and the Beatles.

Title: MACIEJ OBARA: NORTHERN SPACES
Description: Renowned Polish saxophonist Maciej Obara is known for his delicate and lyrical playing style, and he has curated a Scottish super group to join him for the festival’s first international commission. The ECM recording artist will be joined by Harben Kay (saxophone), Seonaid Aitken (fiddle), Su-a Lee (cello), Ben Shankland (piano), Ewan Hastie (bass) and Chun-Wei Kang (drums). Together, they will play a suite of music inspired by the lush landscapes of Scotland and the remarkable architecture of Edinburgh.

Title: CLASSIC JAZZ ORCHESTRA
Description: Friday 24 July, 2-4pmThe Queen's HallThe band that sets the standard for classic jazz, plays a new set of big-bands highlights from the late 1920s to today by way of Basie, Ellington, Benny Carter and Gerry Mulligan. Expect some rarely played gems from this stellar octet featuring Colin Steele (trumpet), Chris Greive (trombone), Dick Lee (saxes/clarinet), Konrad Wiszniewski (saxophone), Martin Foster (saxes/clarinet), Paul Harrison (piano), Roy Percy (bass) and Tom Gordon (drums).

Title: COLIN STEELE: KINGS OF SWING
Description: Trumpeter Colin Steele leads a stellar line-up as he celebrates the swinging dance tunes from the 30s and 40s. Drawing from the likes of Louis Armstrong and Kenny Ball, the band serves up a carefully curated repertoire that showcases the enduring appeal of swing, from its characteristic arrangements to its vibrant rhythms. Expect the very finest jazz played with panache, vibrancy, and freshness.Line up: Colin Steele (trumpet), Martin Foster (reeds), Roy Percy (bass), Campbell Normand (piano), Jim Drummond (drums).

Title: DAVINA & THE VAGABONDS
Description: Davina and The Vagabonds are a long-standing festival favourite. Davina has been compared to the likes of Etta James, Janis Joplin and Billie Holiday, but she’s truly one-of a- kind. She commands the stage from the first note, drawing audiences in with her powerhouse voice, wicked humour and total emotional honesty. Backed by a tight band that play jazz, blues, soul, swing and rock ‘n roll with flair, precision and joy, Davina delivers an evening packed with fearless charisma.

Title: JEEP AND SWEETS
Description: A supergroup fronted by alto saxophonist Martin Kershaw and trumpeter Colin Steele, celebrating the famed musical collaboration between the legendary trumpeter Harry 'Sweets' Edison and saxophonist Johnny Hodges. Both peerless players of their generation whether “cooking with gas”, playing soulful blues or a salacious ballad. The band is completed by Paul Harrison (piano), Andrew Sharkey (bass) and Tom Gordon (drums).

Title: DUTCH JAZZ TALK
Description:
Saturday 18 July, 4.30-5.30pm St Bride's Centre Cafe

Music writer Henning Bolte explores the Dutch jazz scene, uncovering fascinating connections between Scotland and The Netherlands. 

 PART OF SPARK: JAZZ FROM THE NETHERLANDS

Title: HAMISH MCGREGOR & HIS JAZZMEN
Description:
Clarinet virtuoso and traditional jazz band leader extraordinaire, Hamish McGregor pays tribute to Kenny Ball, Chris Barber and Acker Bilk. Featuring Dave Batchelor (trombone) and Roy Percy (bass), this promises a set of all the fun and all the hits!

Charles Dearness (trumpet), Dave Batchelor (trombone/vocals), Hamish McGregor (clarinet/saxophone), Campbell Normand (piano), Roy Percy (bass), Duncan Findlay (guitar/banjo), Alastair Morrow (drums).

Title: FINLAY MCKENZIE QUINTET
Description:
One of Scotland’s most exciting young drummers, Finlay Mackenzie propels his quintet with dynamic soloing and great band interplay. The band made an impressive debut last year and returns with this special new festival commission.

 SUPPORTED BY THE SCOTTISH GOVERNMENT'S EXPO FUND

Title: ENUJSS CONCERT
Description: Led by a team of tutors comprised of leading figures from the Scottish jazz scene, the Edinburgh Napier Jazz Summer School takes place from 20 to 24 July. This final performance offers an opportunity to see and hear the jazz stars of the future as the students show off their newly acquired skills.

Title: ETTA & GLADYS - GLAMOUR & GRIT
Description: Celebrating the raw, bluesy beginnings of Etta James and Gladys Knight, vocal powerhouse Kat Brooks and her extraordinary eight-piece band guide you on a thrilling journey from grit to glamour, paying homage to the fiery spirit and timeless voices of two of music’s greatest legends.

Title: MUD IN YOUR EAR
Description: Acoustic blues wizards Mud In Your Ear specialise in the music of the early pre-war blues masters, as well as in the early electric blues repertoire of Muddy Waters and Elmore James. Featuring Richard O'Donnell (vocals, piano, guitars), Allan Jones (vocals, guitars) and Gary Martin (vocals, harmonica, slide guitar).

Title: BRASS GUMBO
Description: Following their sold out 10 year anniversary show at last year’s festival, Brass Gumbo return with more upbeat, highly danceable arrangements, infusing their trademark blend of New Orleans funk and jazz with tunes from Bowie and the Beatles to Basement Jaxx and Daft Punk.

Title: HIDDEN WAVES QUARTET
Description: Guitarist and composer David Series is joined by a stellar band of Paul Harrison (piano), Elie Afif (bass) and Doug Hough (drums). With compositions influenced by time spent in Northern Spain, the music is inspired and imaginative.

Title: GIRA - SONGS FOR THE ORISHAS
Description: African-Brazilian songs and chants dedicated to the Orishas. The duo features Giulia Drummond’s voice, drums and shruti box with Mario Caribé’s double bass, guitar and percussion.

Title: JAZZ FOR KIDS
Description:
Do you know your scooby doos from your doodats? Learn all about jazz in this fun, interactive workshop for 3 to 5 year-olds led by the brilliant saxophonist Sue McKenzie.

 Ticket price is for a child plus an adult

Title: JAZZ BAR BIG BAND SALUTE OLIVER NELSON
Description:
The talented 17-piece big band pay tribute to American saxophonist and composer Oliver Nelson.

Limited tickets – book early!

Title: JAM SESSION
Description: The classic after hours blow. The top-notch house trio will be joined by a host of talented musicians.

Title: JAZZ FOR KIDS
Description:
Do you know your scooby doos from your doodats? Learn all about jazz in this fun, interactive workshop for 3 to 5 year-olds led by the brilliant saxophonist Sue McKenzie.

 Ticket price is for a child plus an adult

Title: Sisters of the Seas
Description: Two female pirates are condemned to hang for sailing with Calico Jack and terrorising the high seas. Anne Bonny and Mary Read are saved from execution at the last moment, but how? In an age of brutality and adventure, these two outcasts chose to fight alongside and against men. Their pirate careers were short, but their legacy endures. Acting Coach Scotland presents an original theatre show combining physical theatre, music and storytelling to explore the true story of these extraordinary women. Devised by acting graduates, written and directed by Jake Norton in a bold new production.
Venue description: Another high-calibre venue. Two classy spaces, alternatives to the Fringe norm, boasting the most comfortable seats in town! Wonderfully located in our 11-space hub adjacent to theSpaceTriplex and theSpace @ Surgeons' Hall. A programme of music, a capella, theatre, improv, sketch and comedy and a stylish garden bar in the adjacent square. A must for all well-heeled theatre-goers.
Venue accessibility: Staff available to assist, full access via lift facilities. Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Cobbled street around approach but flat pavements avaialble

Title: Hippolytus
Description: What happens when the Queen (really) wants her step son, the Prince? Drums. Movement. Taboo! Euripides' shocking Greek tragedy, Hippolytos, presented in a poetic and percussion-based adaptation by the Burbank H.S. Drama troupe and its award-winning director. Witness this powerful choral work, inspired by theatre icons Jerzy Grotowski, Frederico G Lorca, and Carol Churchill in telling the mythic tale of forbidden love.
Warnings: Contains distressing or potentially triggering themes
Venue description: Nicolson Square Venues
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Jane Harper: Last One Out
Teaser: Australia’s Crime Queen, Jane Harper, is internationally renowned for her atmospheric thrillers. In fact, her 2016 smash hit, The Dry, sparked a whole wave in Aussie publishing of small-town crime fiction, a phenomenon that’s come to be known as ‘Outback Noir’. We’re so excited to welcome Harper to Edinburgh today – hear her chatting about her new novel, Last One Out, a claustrophobic and engrossing study of fractured families and communities. Chaired by Lee Randall.

Title: Writing the Darkness with Patrick Ness
Teaser: Patrick Ness is a titan of Young Adult literature. Author of modern classic, The Knife of Never Letting Go, he returns to the world of the bestselling Chaos Walking trilogy with Piper at the Gates of Dusk. Blending sci-fi, speculative fiction, and adventure, it’s a story of power, division, and hope. Hear Patrick talk about going back to a world he created nearly 20 years ago and what it takes to write award-winning science fiction.

Title: Pen Pals: Jenny Colgan & Mike Gayle
Teaser: The friendship between novelists Jenny Colgan and Mike Gayle constantly yields inspiration and cup-filling conversations. When they met in 2000, Colgan was an unpublished hopeful drawn to Gayle’s first novel, My Legendary Girlfriend, and their mutual reverence for romance. Since then, she’s sold 15 million books and he’s won the Romantic Novelists’ Association Outstanding Achievement Award. Today, they chat about the importance of friends who not only understand your craft but have your back. Chaired by Claire Urquhart.

Title: Tim Wu: The Age of Extraction
Teaser: Professor at Columbia Law School, special assistant to President Biden for technology and competition policy, and inventor of the term ‘net neutrality’ – Tim Wu’s work places him at the cutting edge of legal and ethical questions about the new information age. Joining us with The Age of Extraction, he breaks down the accelerating quest to extract data, attention, and profit from us, as well as how to break the tech monopoly and bring prosperity for all. Chaired by Malcolm Borthwick.

Title: Philippe Sands & Colm Tóibín: Remembering the Dirty War
Teaser: From 1976 until 1983, the Argentine military junta’s Dirty War was a brutal campaign of violence – tens of thousands of citizens ‘disappeared’, murdered by the state. 50 years on, join Brooklyn author Colm Tóibín – whose 1996 novel, The Story of the Night, was inspired by his own experiences in Argentina – and international lawyer and East West Street author Philippe Sands as they consider the long-lasting impact of the war.

Title: Simukai Chigudu: Chasing Freedom
Teaser: Oxford University’s associate professor of African politics, Simukai Chigudu is part of the ‘Born Free’ generation, raised as colonial rule ended in Zimbabwe. In Chasing Freedom, he details a childhood steeped in Britishness – from Shakespeare to cricket – before being forced to leave the country as it descended into political violence and economic collapse. Join Chigudu discussing his remarkable story: that of a boy shaped through his parents’ stories and by the great currents of late 20th century history. Chaired by Dina Nayeri.

Title: Francis Spufford: Nonesuch
Teaser: To read Francis Spufford’s literary fantasy Nonesuch is to be grabbed by the hand and pulled, screaming with delight, through a version of wartime London where statues talk, timelines bend, and fascism entangles with dark magic. From Booker-longlisted Light Perpetual to his last novel Cahokia Jazz, Spufford is always deft at drawing timely truths out of alternate realities. If you need a fresh perspective on how to keep fighting the good fight, don’t miss him. Chaired by Chitra Ramaswamy.

Title: John Lanchester & Alexander Starritt: Work/Life Balance
Teaser: Two masters of observational fiction come together to explore why our feelings around work and money can reveal the deepest truths. Alexander Starritt’s Drayton and Mackenzie, a friendship epic about two entrepreneurs, was the first novel in 15 years to grace the Financial Times’s Business Book of the Year longlist, while John Lanchester’s black comedy, Look What You Made Me Do, poses the question: is it ever ethical to profit from another person’s pain? Chaired by Zoe Venditozzi. Supported by Claire & Mark Urquhart.

Title: Fatima Bhutto: Gaza – The Story of a Genocide
Teaser: Edited by Fatima Bhutto and Sonia Faleiro, Gaza: The Story of a Genocide is an urgent, powerful collection of personal testimony, poetry, art, and frontline reportage, bearing witness to the vast, ongoing destruction inflicted on Palestine. Today, Bhutto is joined by some of the collection’s award-winning contributors, including Tareq Baconi and Ahmed Masoud, to reflect on their pieces and experiences, the horror of existing under current conditions, and what future lies ahead for the Palestinian people. Check back soon for the full line-up.

Outside Black Thorn Tattoo, Books N Cup and the Post Office on Home Street

Next to The Bike Station on Lauriston Place

By Car

Venue Accessibility



Physical Access to the Cameo



Both the bar and main entrance are wheelchair accessible. However, level access to the bar is only available from the street through the Lochrin Place entrance – moving between the two areas requires a wheelchair user to enter via the street.



Physical Access in the Screening Rooms



Screens 1 and 2 are accessible to customers with limited mobility, including wheelchair users. There are four wheelchair spaces in Screen 1 and two in Screen 2.



Dedicated wheelchair spaces are available in the following locations:



Screen 1: Row M, Seats 1-2 & 20-21



Screen 2: Row A, Seats 5-6 & 10-11



Aisles in our screens are located on each side of every row:



Screen 1: aisles are located next to seats A1 – M21 or seats A20, C20, E20, G20, J20, L20.



Screen 2: aisles are located next to seats A1-C1, A15, B16, and C18.



Sofa seats are double seats with no armrest in between. These are sold as two seats and are located:



Screen 1: No sofa seats



Screen 2: B1+2, B3+4, B13+14, B15+16, C1+2, C3+4, C15+16, C17+18



All seats have immovable armrests, and chairs are fixed together.



The distance of the aisles between seats – from the front of one row of seats to the back of another – is approximately 50cm. The seat base and back are approx 48cm wide; 69cm wide including armrests.



The sofa seats base and back are approximately 110cm wide; 133cm wide including armrests. These are sold as two separate seats.



Audio



All three screens are fitted with the Williams Sound hearing assistance headset system; please notify a member of staff if you wish to use a headset or induction loop compatible with a hearing aid.



Toilets



There is a fully accessible separate toilet for wheelchair users opposite the doors to Screen 1. There is an emergency call-point (the red hanging cord) inside should you need to call for assistance.



Assistance dogs



Assistance dogs are welcome at The Cameo Picturehouse. If you wish to take a dog into a performance, please let us know once you have booked your tickets, so we can ensure an aisle seat is reserved for you.



The Meadows is very close by for the exercise of assistance dogs. 



The bar is dog friendly and staff can provide water bowls and treats if the dogs are allowed.

Screen 2: Row A, Seats 5-6 & 10-11

Audio



All three screens are fitted with the Williams Sound hearing assistance headset system; please notify a member of staff if you wish to use a headset or induction loop compatible with a hearing aid.

Description: Four teenagers wake in a room that feels strangely familiar. None of them remember how they got there or recognise one another. Inviting audiences of all ages to reflect on the moments that quietly shape who we become.

Title: Her Private Hell
Description: Glamorous young actresses are targeted by the killer Leather Man and a vengeful GI searches for his daughter in this hypnotic, ultraviolent film from Nicolas Winding Refn. Set against the backdrop of a surreal, neon soaked city, a bizarre high rise hotel, the violent streets of retrofuturist urban sprawl and extravagant film production sets, this strange, unsettling and deeply beautiful neo-Giallo is an exercise in gleeful filmmaking style. A terrific, pounding new score from regular Brian DePalma collaborator Pino Donaggio is the icing on the cake for fans of psychedelic cinema and baroque excess. Quite simply this is pure cinema. – Paul Ridd

Title: Future Library

Title: Louise Newson: The Power of Hormones
Teaser: When it comes to women’s health, there’s a long and harmful history of misdiagnosis, medical blindness, and complacency. In today’s myth-busting conversation, hormone specialist Dr Louise Newson – a leading authority on menopause care, as well as a Sunday Times bestselling author, host of the UK’s no.1 medical podcast (The Dr Louise Newson Podcast), and founder of the Balance app – unpacks her bold new book, The Power of Hormones. Kylie Reid – founder and director of Scottish women’s network, egg – chairs this insightful, urgent discussion about how better understanding our hormones could radically transform our lives.

Title: Meet the Winners: International Booker Prize 2026
Teaser: Over scenic train rides and braised pork rice, a Japanese novelist in 1930s Taiwan falls for the interpreter hired to guide her. Yáng Shuāng-zǐ's Taiwan Travelogue, translated by Lin King, disguises itself as a rediscovered text within a text, weaving together queer desire, postcolonial critique, hilarious dialogue, and sumptuous food writing.In May this year, the novel won 2026’s International Booker Prize (supported by Bukhman Philanthropies): the world’s most influential award for translated fiction, championing literature from around the world and fostering an engaged global community of writers and readers whose experiences transcend national borders. The award brings international attention to both the author and translator with the prize divided equally between them.Join us today as Emeritus Director Fiammetta Rocco speaks to both author and translator, Yáng and King, about appetite and longing, translation and history, and the politics of our most intimate encounters.

Title: Rana Dasgupta & Ece Temelkuran: Crossing Borders

Title: Eyal Weizman: Ungrounding
Teaser: Director of the organisation Forensic Architecture, Eyal Weizman is a world-leading expert on the relationship between conflict and the built and natural environments. Since 2023, the group has worked to produce evidence for the International Court of Justice’s genocide case against Israel, using architectural and territorial analysis. In Ungrounding, he unveils a chilling insider’s view of the history and 'deep cartography' of the war, unflinchingly cataloging the campaigns of violence and displacement that have reshaped Gaza. Join him for an eye-opening discussion on how the new interdisciplinary field of forensic architecture is used to uncover the truth. Chaired by Leonie Bell.

Title: Pierrepoint: The People's Hangman
Description: Albert Pierrepoint was an English hangman who executed an estimated 435 people in a 25-year career with HMP Prisons between the 1930s and 1950s. During his tenure, he was responsible for the executions of several high-profile murderers including the Acid Bath Killer – John Haigh, and Ruth Ellis – the last woman to be hung in England. Another was the case of one John Reginald Christie of 10 Rillington Place infamy. Through the executioner's eyes, this theatrical production dissects and scrutinises Christie's crimes and examines how he came to be on the end of a rope.

PART OF THE ANDERSON OPERA SERIES

Greek tragedy meets modern psychology in Richard Strauss’s audacious opera.
Description: PART OF THE ANDERSON OPERA SERIESGreek tragedy meets modern psychology in Richard Strauss’s audacious opera. Elektra is determined to avenge the murder of her father Agamemnon by her mother Klytämnestra – but will Klytämnestra destroy her first?Strauss evokes his characters’ larger-than-life emotions through massive orchestral forces and daring harmonies. Leading dramatic sopranos Ingela Brimberg and Nina Stemme perform the virtuoso roles of Elektra and Klytämnestra.  The Anderson Opera Series, made possible by James and Morag Anderson, allows the Festival to bring internationally acclaimed opera to Edinburgh and ensures these unmissable performances remain accessible to the widest possible audience with additional support from the Embassy of Sweden in LondonSung in German with English surtitles

Description:
We’re kicking off Falastin Film Festival this year with a party, bringing together Palestinian and local artists for a night not to be missed! We have three amazing acts lined up: Mo’min Swaitat (Palestinian Sound Archive), Hajar Ibrahim (Shahrazadi duo) and Eclair Fifi! Get ready to dance your heart out to an eclectic mix, including Palestinian and Arabic celebratory music, wedding field recordings, hip hop, electro, and revolutionary songs from Palestine and beyond.

About the DJs: 

Mo’min Swaitat:Through his project, Palestinian Sound Archive, Mo’min has been determined to preserve Palestinian audio history. For the past five years, Swaitat has been introducing audiences from all around the world to Palestinian musical archives while situating it in its cultural, social, and political contexts.

Hajar Ibrahim:Part of the formerly Edinburgh-based Shahrazadi duo, Hajar is Palestinian-Egyptian, grew up in Lebanon and is excited to return to FFF to play dynamic tunes from the SWANA region – as always, inspired by azadi: freedom.

Eclair Fifi:

A Scottish DJ, producer and visual artist celebrated for her unique blend of musical styles. With her deep understanding of genres such as Italo, Latin freestyle, electro, hip hop and house, she brings versatility and energy to every set.

Description: Outstanding vocal ensemble The Gesualdo Six explores the chilling music and life story of composer Carlo Gesualdo in a multi-media concert piece.What do we do with the art of monstrous people? The 16th-century composer Carlo Gesualdo is infamous for murdering his wife and her lover, while also being remembered for his dissonant musical language.  Director Bill Barclay has chosen some of Gesualdo’s darkest music, including Tenebrae (a mass for the composer’s own death), to create a fascinating but chilling portrait of the composer. The Gesualdo Six sing with ‘precision, pure tone and nuanced expression’ (The Guardian), joined by six actor-dancers to further illustrate the music through Renaissance iconography, puppetry and sinister tableaux vivants.  Death of Gesualdo contrasts beauty and monstrosity in a completely unique experience.  According to a recent five-star review, 'the staging, the singing and acting are sublime' (The Times).While the pristine sounds of this concert can be enjoyed throughout the hall, please note that side seats will have less direct views of some of the theatrical elements. Screen 1: Row M, Seats 1-2 & 20-21



Screen 2: Row A, Seats 5-6 & 10-11

Screen 2: aisles are located next to seats A1-C1, A15, B16, and C18.

Screen 1: No sofa seats



Screen 2: B1+2, B3+4, B13+14, B15+16, C1+2, C3+4, C15+16, C17+18

The sofa seats base and back are approximately 110cm wide; 133cm wide including armrests. These are sold as two separate seats.



Audio

The Meadows is very close by for the exercise of assistance dogs.

Description: Dan Daw returns to the Festival with his bold and triumphant dance-theatre workHow do you continue to value yourself when society doesn’t value you? EXXY (Australian slang for, ‘that’s expensive, mate’) takes us back to where queer, disabled artist Dan Daw began – working class, with very little.Dan returns to the Festival after last year’s The Dan Daw Show, this time joined by three extraordinary performers who move like him. Together, they conjure up the tantalising possibility of blending in after a lifetime of standing out. With raw honesty and scorching stagecraft, they ask what it costs to stay at the top of your game when you’ve always been made to feel on the outside.  Visually provocative and threaded with humour, EXXY refuses to offer easy answers. Instead, it invites us into the contradictions Dan Daw embodies: bold yet insecure, triumphant yet uncertain, longing for community, yet determined to be one of a kind. Before each performance there will be an Access Drop-In session. Description:
Sound performance Zifzafa, named for an Arabic word describing a wind that shakes everything in its path, centres on the Israeli-occupied Syrian Golan Heights, where 30 planned wind turbines will flood the region with a relentless mechanical roar. Framed as a ‘green’ energy project, the turbines weaponise sound itself, unsettling and exhausting local life. 

Lawrence Abu Hamdan, artist and founder of Earshot, the first non-profit dedicated to audio for justice, whose investigations have informed landmark legal cases, brings this research to the stage. The performance is scored by Busher Kanj Abu Saleh, who performs live together with saxophonist Amr Mdah and Renate Lurdesa Baumane. Through sound and visual models, they turn the imposed noise into an act of resistance: transforming acoustic violence into something that can be witnessed, felt, and collectively opposed.

The performance is programmed in collaboration with Falastin Film Festival, and accompanied by an exhibition at The Common Guild in Glasgow, running 20 Aug—17 October.

Join us after the performance at Leith Theatre to close out the festival with a pop-up bar hosted by festival partners, Whitebox.

Description:

Teaser: Join 'some of the best young orchestral players in America' (The New York Times), in the second year of our collaboration with Carnegie Hall.
Description: Join 'some of the best young orchestral players in America' (The New York Times), in the second year of our collaboration with Carnegie Hall. The exceptional National Youth Orchestra of the United States of America performs three vibrant 20th-century masterpieces. These talented young musicians are joined by Festival regular, American conductor Karina Canellakis, praised by Gramophone for her ‘finesse and fire’. Samuel Barber’s effervescent Overture to The School for Scandal is followed by George Gershwin’s Piano Concerto, which brings the energetic rhythms of jazz dances and the soulful sound of American blues into the classical arena. Virtuoso pianist Kirill Gerstein, described by Tagesspiel as ‘a real phenomenon’, joins as the soloist.  The concert closes with Béla Bartók’s Concerto for Orchestra – his final, and most popular, orchestral work. The Concerto sprung from a period of darkness in Bartók’s life, while he was living in exile in the US and suffering from illness and poverty. Yet, when the conductor Serge Koussevistzky visited him in hospital to commission this piece, Bartók went on to write this alternately nostalgic, witty and joyful tribute to his native Hungary, which is now a hallmark of classical music repertoire. Pre-Performance Information 🎶Arrive early to enjoy two new compositions from Carnegie Hall's young composters, performed by Edinburgh Youth Orchestra.As part of an ongoing transatlantic collaboration between Carnegie Hall's Young Composers and the Edinburgh Youth Orchestra there will be performances taking place on the steps of Usher Hall and in the Upper Circle Bar before the start of the NYO show from 6:40-7:20pm.They perform Orini for Wind Sextet by Ethan Hsu and Acid for String Quartet by Henry Golden.Supported by Dunard Fund

Title: JLCO plays Duke Ellington
Teaser: A rare opportunity to experience Duke Ellington’s monumental jazz symphony, Black, Brown and Beige.
Description: A rare opportunity to experience Duke Ellington’s monumental jazz symphony, Black, Brown and Beige. Duke Ellington’s Black, Brown and Beige weaves the sounds of blues, spirituals and work songs into a suite for jazz orchestra. Ellington, troubled by clichéd representations of Black culture, felt it was ‘time a big piece was written from the inside’. His ambitious suite gives a powerful account of Black life in America, from slavery, through emancipation, segregation and military service, to a new era of prosperity and cultural assertiveness. In the years since its 1943 premiere, Black, Brown and Beige has been hailed as a remarkable musical and political statement. Wynton Marsalis and the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra recently released a definitive recording of the work.  JLCO trombonist Chris Crenshaw conducts and Ekep Nkwelle joins to sing the haunting, melancholy ‘Blues theme mauve’. The orchestra is also joined by emerging stars of the American jazz scene, who will curate a surprise programme to complement Ellington’s masterpiece.    Sung in English with surtitles Running order to be announced on the night. The day after the performance, you’ll find the full repertoire and order listed on this webpage.

Description: UK PREMIEREVisionary Brazilian director Christiane Jatahy returns to the Festival with a radical sequel to Henrik Ibsen’s An Enemy of the People, featuring Golden Globe-winning actor Wagner Moura.Christiane Jatahy picks up where Ibsen left off.  In Ibsen's groundbreaking 1882 play, An Enemy of the People, protagonist Thomas Stockmann faces shame and exile after attempting to expose a water pollution scandal in his hometown. More than a century later, Ibsen’s work remains urgent, grappling with the conflict between personal integrity and social conformity.Jatahy’s sequel throws Stockmann, played by Golden Globe-winning actor Wagner Moura (Narcos, The Secret Agent), into a modern-day public courtroom to determine his fate. Lawyers and judges are noticeably absent, and it’s up to a jury of audience members to decide if he is innocent or whether he is indeed an ‘enemy of the people’. Transplanting Ibsen’s themes to contemporary Brazil, A Trial – after An Enemy of the People offers a sharp look at authoritarianism, fake news and public judgement. Ever inventive and deeply political, Jatahy combines audience participation and filmed footage, creating a one-of-a-kind performance each night where the line between reality and fiction is constantly blurred.A special collaboration between Edinburgh International Festival, Festival d'Avignon and Holland Festival, the three European festivals established in 1947.Audience ParticipationEach night, 11 people who register before the performance are randomly selected to serve as the jury. They have the power to decide on Stockmann's guilt, playing a pivotal role in shaping the ending of the play.Supported by Edinburgh International Festival Endowment Fundwith additional support from the Consulate General of Brazil in Edinburgh and Instituto Guimarães RosaPerformed in Portuguese and English with English surtitles.

Description: Enjoy a programme of 20th-century French chamber music.Wind soloists from the Scottish Chamber Orchestra explore music from Poulenc, Ravel and Françaix, with their conductor Maxim Emelyanychev on piano. Francis Poulenc’s chamber music is a beguiling mix of lyrical and frenetic, sombre and playful. Written the year before he died, the sonatas for oboe and clarinet take an occasionally melancholic look back at his musical life, quoting from both early and more recent works. The famous Flute Sonata retains its power to charm, yet is infused with memories of a lost loved one. In contrast, the much earlier Sextet bursts out of the blocks with astonishing, effervescent energy. Dazzling piano music from Maurice Ravel and Jean Françaix’s bustling ‘Musique de Brasserie’ – a vivid portrait of a busy Parisian restaurant – add to this enthralling, colourful, and thoroughly French concert.

Venue Accessibility



Physical Access to the Cameo



Both the bar and main entrance are wheelchair accessible. However, level access to the bar is only available from the street through the Lochrin Place entrance – moving between the two areas requires a wheelchair user to enter via the street.



Physical Access in the Screening Rooms



Screens 1 and 2 are accessible to customers with limited mobility, including wheelchair users. There are four wheelchair spaces in Screen 1 and two in Screen 2.



Dedicated wheelchair spaces are available in the following locations:



Screen 1: Row M, Seats 1-2 & 20-21



Screen 2: Row A, Seats 5-6 & 10-11



Aisles in our screens are located on each side of every row:



Screen 1: aisles are located next to seats A1 – M21 or seats A20, C20, E20, G20, J20, L20.



Screen 2: aisles are located next to seats A1-C1, A15, B16, and C18.



Sofa seats are double seats with no armrest in between. These are sold as two seats and are located:



Screen 1: No sofa seats



Screen 2: B1+2, B3+4, B13+14, B15+16, C1+2, C3+4, C15+16, C17+18



All seats have immovable armrests, and chairs are fixed together.



The distance of the aisles between seats – from the front of one row of seats to the back of another – is approximately 50cm. The seat base and back are approx 48cm wide; 69cm wide including armrests.



The sofa seats base and back are approximately 110cm wide; 133cm wide including armrests. These are sold as two separate seats.



Audio



All three screens are fitted with the Williams Sound hearing assistance headset system; please notify a member of staff if you wish to use a headset or induction loop compatible with a hearing aid.



Toilets



There is a fully accessible separate toilet for wheelchair users opposite the doors to Screen 1. There is an emergency call-point (the red hanging cord) inside should you need to call for assistance.



Assistance dogs



Assistance dogs are welcome at The Cameo Picturehouse. If you wish to take a dog into a performance, please let us know once you have booked your tickets, so we can ensure an aisle seat is reserved for you.



The Meadows is very close by for the exercise of assistance dogs. 



The bar is dog friendly and staff can provide water bowls and treats if the dogs are allowed.
