Title: Xiao Hai: Adrift in the South
Teaser: China's migrant workers’ literature movement has seen a boom in recent years, with fascinating autobiographical works produced by writers involved in the nation’s gig and service economy. Xiao Hai’s Adrift in the South is a landmark memoir in this movement, offering a first-hand account of a decade spent moving between cities and factory jobs. Today, the essayist and poet provides a rare perspective on survival, dignity, and the human cost of the country's economic rise. Chaired by Anthony Tao.

Title: My Mum Accidentally Set Me Up With A Married Woman
Description: A saleswoman knocked on my family’s door. My mum got her number, and insisted I asked the woman out. I was single, desperate and living with my parents. We started dating and things were going well. My mum thought we were going to get married. The problem was, this woman was already married. This stand-up comedy show explains it all.

Description: BENCHES is a free, immersive exhibition celebrating neurodivergent creativity through the lens of autistic amateur photographer Tim Hart. They bring us today’s two-part performance, introducing Noh Theatre in Part One with a piece based on the oldest novel of all time, followed by a new and contemporary collaboration blending Scottish and Japanese folklore, myth and music in Part Two. This performance is repeated on Tue 25 Aug at 19:00 Part One: Nonomiya (Wildwood Shrine) (15th century) Nonomiya is a masterwork of Noh theatre, written by Konparu Zenchiku in the 15th century, based on the 11th century classic, The Tale of Genji by Murasaki Shikibu. This performance presents the famous second act, in which the spirit of Lady Rokujō reveals her lingering passion and sorrow. Part Two: Song of Rona Island (2025) A once-in-a-lifetime chance to experience the groundbreaking union of Scottish culture and the 600-year-old art of Japanese Noh theatre, inspired by former Makar Kathleen Jamie’s essay ‘On Rona’ from her collection, Sightlines. Through dialogue, chant, dance, and music, five Noh performers and Scots musicians Aidan O’Rourke and Brìghde Chaimbeul take us on an ecological journey to an abandoned Hebridean island to discover its haunting past. Part of Scotland to the World. Supported by Sir Ewan and Lady Brown, The British Council, and The Great Britain Sasakawa Foundation.Photography credit: Ken Yoshikoshi

Description: Two women, two cages. In 1898, a young woman in late Qing China is bound by lotus shoes and arranged marriage. In Victorian England, another is trapped by hysteria and a husband’s law. Separated by geography but mirrored on stage across a transparent divide, their lives unfold side by side from girlhood, through marriage, mirroring each other in a fierce exploration of forbidden love, forced obedience and the dangerous hope of escape. This dark, poetic, cross-cultural drama is for audiences who love intimate new writing, feminist history and stories that refuse to stay silent.

Divorced, and back in her childhood bedroom at 30, Sundance award-winning actress and NYC stand-up Alessandra Ford (Shameless, Greenberg, Plainclothes) confronts the absurd humiliation of starting over. And for the grand finale, the audience inspire Cunliffe with their favourite pop, jazz and classical requests, as he improvises an original composition on the spot. Don’t miss this astonishing solo adventure!

Title: Make Yourself at Home
Description: Make Yourself at Home follows Michael, a man struggling with agoraphobia at the height of his anxiety. After losing his girlfriend, Michael attempts to heal in the confines of his home. An absurd, darkly comic new play with an electrifying score, Nesting is a visceral exploration of love, death and duty from Trolley Problem, following their sold-out production of Mistero Buffo at the Citizens Theatre.

Venue accessibility: We are committed to making your visit to Summerhall an enjoyable experience and we are working to make our venue as accessible as possible. Our step-free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. From here, The Royal Dick pub is situated to your right as you come in (with ramp access entry to bar behind the pub) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads you up to the left and into the building where you can access our reception, boutique, cafe and some of our venues. We have lift access to some of the first floor spaces and the basement spaces. Further information about individual spaces and shows can be obtained from the box office. If you would like more information about the accessibility of particular shows, please contact us by phone on 0131 560 6243 or by email on boxoffice@summerhallarts.co.uk. Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with, please do not hesitate to ask. www.summerhallarts.co.uk/accessibility/. Wheelchair accessible toilets can be found in the Royal Dick pub and on the Ground floor by the cafe. Although there is no on-site parking at Summerhall, especially during the Fringe, paid parking spaces are available on the nearby Sciennes Road. Please be aware that parking is limited and can be quite competitive. Title: Step One
Description: One chair. One question. Sit with us for a moment. In this gentle one-to-one encounter, you’re invited to share an idea you’ve always wanted to try, but haven’t yet. Step One is a quiet participatory artwork by Short Supply, exploring the moment before something begins. Each meeting lasts a few minutes and unfolds differently depending on who sits down. In the middle of the Edinburgh Fringe, this piece offers a pause from the noise – a space to reflect, speak freely and acknowledge the ideas we carry but rarely say out loud.

Title: A Pebble in the Road
Description: Internationally renowned star of stage and screen, Ingeborga Dapkunaite gives a spontaneous, child's-eye account of three generations of women through a hundred turbulent, Lithuanian years. As Grandad Stasys used to say: 'You should speak the languages of your neighbours because you never know who's going to march in and when'. Joyful, haunting and evocative. Taking the lead in the Oscar winner, Burnt By The Sun, Ingeborga has made over a hundred films. She has played major theatres in Europe, the USA, Russia, Australia, several in London's West End and elsewhere.

Title: Mario Adrion: Live a Little
Description: A darkly funny show about a boy from a picturesque German town who leaves it all behind to become an international fashion model. Armed with a need for approval, Mario dives headfirst into the modelling world, navigating the chaos of pseudo professional relationships, the European runway, and sketchy modelling gigs. Along the way, Mario faces unhealthy power dynamics, constant rejection, and significant sexual abuse within the industry. The show explores themes of self-love, the need for acceptance, and grappling with sexual trauma from a male perspective. It’s a story about being hot — and sad.

Title: ArounD the WorlD in 80 ToyS
Description: A surprising hybrid of theatre and film that is at once highly theatrical and wonderfully cinematic. Paris, 1925. In a tiny toy shop inside the Montparnasse train station, film and special effects pioneer Georges Méliès, now forgotten, faces eviction. A toy comes to life. Using hidden cameras, a movie screen, miniatures and magic, Georges creates an epic cinematic universe and voyage that leads to his rediscovery. Theatrical wizard Thaddeus Phillips 'could have been a great silent-movie comedian' (New York Times) and 80 eclectic vintage toys star in this visually stunning tour de force.

Venue description: Set in the iconic former Veterinary College, Summerhall Arts' programme is packed full of exciting and challenging theatre, dance, visual art and music from across the world and Scotland. Full programme available at summerhallarts.co.uk.
Venue accessibility: We are committed to making your visit to Summerhall an enjoyable experience and we are working to make our venue as accessible as possible. The building is B-listed and is over one hundred years old and not all of our spaces are fully accessible. If coming into Summerhall using the main entrance, please be aware that there are nine steps up to reception and the steps do not have a handrail. Our step-free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. From here, The Royal Dick pub is situated to your right as you come in (with ramp access entry to bar behind the pub) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads you up to the left and into the building where you can access our reception, boutique, cafe and some of our venues. We have lift access to some of the first floor spaces and the basement spaces. Further information about individual spaces and shows can be obtained from the box office. If you would like more information about the accessibility of particular shows, please contact us by phone on 0131 560 6243 or by email on boxoffice@summerhallarts.co.uk. Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with, please do not hesitate to ask. www.summerhallarts.co.uk/accessibility/. Wheelchair accessible toilets can be found in the Royal Dick pub and on the Ground floor by the cafe. Although there is no on-site parking at Summerhall, especially during the Fringe, paid parking spaces are available on the nearby Sciennes Road. Please be aware that parking is limited and can be quite competitive. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. There are 9 steps up to the main entrance of Summerhall, these steps do not have a handrail. Wheelchair and limited-mobility access is via the side entrance on Summerhall Square which is clearly marked by the large vehicle gates. This captivating show takes audiences on a journey through Glen Campbell’s remarkable career, from his humble beginnings to his rise as Grammy-winning artist and global superstar. Featuring live performances of Glen's most iconic hits, including Rhinestone Cowboy, Wichita Lineman, By the Time I Get to Phoenix and many more, the show blends heart-warming storytelling and authentic musical arrangements.

Seriously unserious, devoutly disobedient, still refusing to buy, sell or process anything. Now a Zen-punk dissident duct-taping ancient wisdom to the collapse of the American empire, with deep gratitude and zero credentials, like a sticky note saying: "Be kind. Rewind. Revolt." Join Lloyd in a kinda-sorta guided meditation to survive late-stage effin' everything... Like a vinyl record spinning in a microwave of manifest destiny, humming: "Oh well. Never-mind." Written/performed by Dennis Trainor Jr (Manifest Destiny's Child), directed by Olivier winner Guy Masterson.

Taking the action, pyrotechnics and stunt work to new levels for the series, this ambitious new entry is an adrenalin pumping, profane delight, sure to delight fans with its mix of cheerfully brutish action and witty gutter dialogue, as well as bring new audiences to the franchise. -Paul Ridd

Venue description:
Cameo Picturehouse



38 Home Street, EH3 9LZ



What 3 Words location: ///finger.images.smashes







Getting Here



By Bus and Tram



Lothian Bus routes 10, 11, 15, 15a, 16, 23, 27, 45 all serve the area of Tollcross on a regular basis.



Download the Lothian Buses/ Edinburgh Trams and Borders Buses app on App Store or Google Play to plan your journey, buy tickets and keep up to date with the latest service alerts. 



By Train



Cameo Picturehouse is a twenty-minute walk from Haymarket Station, and a twenty-five minute walk from Waverley Station. 



Refer to National Rail for timetables and tickets. 



By Bike 



Cameo Picturehouse is located just off the National Cycle Network route 75. There are several bike parking locations nearby:




Outside Black Thorn Tattoo, Books N Cup and the Post Office on Home Street



Opposite the entrance to Tollcross Fire Station



Next to The Bike Station on Lauriston Place 








Refer to Edinburgh City Council’s cycling and walking guide for more information about the routes and a detailed map of the cycle parking locations. 



By Car



The nearest multi-storey car park to Cameo Picturehouse is Princes Exchange, accessible via Riego Street. 



Princes Exchange | EH3 9BL



What 3 Words for car park entrance location: ///skill.fats.things



146 spaces



Due to the city centre location there is very limited on-street parking with time restrictions. 



Refer to Edinburgh City Council’s parking guide for more information and on-street parking locations and accessible parking bays. 







Venue Accessibility



Physical Access to the Cameo



Both the bar and main entrance are wheelchair accessible. However, level access to the bar is only available from the street through the Lochrin Place entrance – moving between the two areas requires a wheelchair user to enter via the street.



Physical Access in the Screening Rooms



Screens 1 and 2 are accessible to customers with limited mobility, including wheelchair users. There are four wheelchair spaces in Screen 1 and two in Screen 2.



Dedicated wheelchair spaces are available in the following locations:



Screen 1: Row M, Seats 1-2 & 20-21



Screen 2: Row A, Seats 5-6 & 10-11



Aisles in our screens are located on each side of every row:



Screen 1: aisles are located next to seats A1 – M21 or seats A20, C20, E20, G20, J20, L20.



Screen 2: aisles are located next to seats A1-C1, A15, B16, and C18.



Sofa seats are double seats with no armrest in between. These are sold as two seats and are located:



Screen 1: No sofa seats



Screen 2: B1+2, B3+4, B13+14, B15+16, C1+2, C3+4, C15+16, C17+18



All seats have immovable armrests, and chairs are fixed together.



The distance of the aisles between seats – from the front of one row of seats to the back of another – is approximately 50cm. The seat base and back are approx 48cm wide; 69cm wide including armrests.



The sofa seats base and back are approximately 110cm wide; 133cm wide including armrests. These are sold as two separate seats.



Audio



All three screens are fitted with the Williams Sound hearing assistance headset system; please notify a member of staff if you wish to use a headset or induction loop compatible with a hearing aid.



Toilets



There is a fully accessible separate toilet for wheelchair users opposite the doors to Screen 1. There is an emergency call-point (the red hanging cord) inside should you need to call for assistance.



Assistance dogs



Assistance dogs are welcome at The Cameo Picturehouse. If you wish to take a dog into a performance, please let us know once you have booked your tickets, so we can ensure an aisle seat is reserved for you.



The Meadows is very close by for the exercise of assistance dogs. 



The bar is dog friendly and staff can provide water bowls and treats if the dogs are allowed.







Further Information



Cameo Picturehouse contact details



By Phone: Picturehouse’s dedicated accessibility line 02072 947908 (Text Relay call 18001 02072 947908).



By Email: Use the email form on Picturehouse’s website here.

Title: A Wolf Shall Devour the Sun
Description: Respected by ancient cultures but the archetypal villain in European fairy tales, wolves were hunted to extinction in Scotland by the 18th century. Ancient myth, mesmeric imagery and dreamlike soundscapes open a liminal space where Norse gods, Irish shapeshifters and Siberian wolf-children traverse Scottish moors and Transylvanian mountains. Live music stirs the soul. Shadow puppetry and animation portray terror and playfulness. Stories about our oldest ally ask: in the absence of the wolf, what is lost? Originally commissioned by the Scottish International Storytelling Festival 2024. 'Powerful and magical' **** (List). 'Richly textured' **** (CorrBlimey.uk).

Up against arms traffickers, the CIA, some familiar foes and a seemingly endless parade of tough-talking gangsters, Tate battles to remain the last man standing in this stylish action spectacle. Title: Iliad: The Song of Thetis
Description: An incendiary retelling of Homer’s Iliad, sung through the voice of Thetis, Achilles’ mother. Two performers fluidly shifting: god/mortal, mother/warrior, goddess/lover, masculine/feminine, collapsing the boundaries of gender, power and fate. Love – maternal, erotic, spiritual – collides with the brutal machinery of war. Developed through international residencies and informed by artistic exchange with Lebanese and Palestinian artists working amid ongoing conflict, the production refuses nostalgia. Olympus is not distant; it is political, volatile, human. Nearly three millennia later, the epic burns with the same question: who wages war, and who pays the price?

Title: Industry Talk: Unmaking the Colonial Gaze in Cinema
Description:
Edinburgh-based, bi-racial British Chinese filmmaker Paul Sng, director of last year’s EIFF closer Reality is not Enough, presents an innovative session that will discuss the generational impacts of colonialism on the moving image and ask what value judgments determine which films from marginalised communities receive mainstream funding, distribution and exhibition? The panel will examine cinema’s colonial legacy, its lasting influence on representation and industry inequality. Moving beyond critique, the conversation will focus on how contemporary filmmakers can actively decolonise their practice.



Hosted by Paul Sng with panellists including filmmakers Campbell X and Raisah Ahmad and Anthony Andrews of We Are Parable.

Title: Pilgrims
Description: 'Does there always have to be a girl? Does she always have to be the prize?' Hailed as provocative, poetic and playwrighting at its peak, this haunting drama, by award-winning writer Elinor Cook, tells of a very modern love-triangle: between feminist academic Rachel, and mountaineering prodigies Dan and Will. Tracing their interwoven trajectories, Pilgrims dramatises the conflicting attractions of freedom and belonging, and interrogates inherited assumptions about gender, storytelling and nature. How far do we all remain trapped in narratives beyond our own making? What might escape cost us? And what better stories do we have to guide us?

Title: Coming Home
Description: A US Marine Corps captain’s wife (Jane Fonda) finds herself drawn to a paraplegic war vet (Jon Voight) after her husband (Bruce Dern) leaves to fight in Vietnam. When her husband returns from the front, each one of them has changed immeasurably. Conceived and produced by Fonda, Coming Home is one of the earliest films to explore emotional as well as physical consequences of the Vietnam War. Hal Ashby’s compassionate, insightful indictment of the conflict's impact is an authentic, richly observed and deeply moving exploration of disillusionment, guilt and complex trauma, featuring extraordinary performances from its Oscar-winning cast.

When a wealthy grandmother enrols her granddaughters, including 15-year-old Jane Cumming, the school’s fragile balance begins to shift. Jane’s isolation, the teachers’ concern and the pressures of respectability soon lead to an accusation that changes all their lives. Based on true events, Sophie Heldman’s beautifully made period drama explores prejudice, reputation and the cost of surviving in a strict and unforgiving society.

Title: Sexy Beast
Description: 25 years since its UK release, EIFF presents a brand-new restoration of Jonathan Glazer’s (The Zone of Interest, Under the Skin) searing directorial debut. When retired gangster Gal (Winstone) is unwillingly approached by his sociopathic former boss (Kingsley) to undertake one last job, a tense, psychological game of cat and mouse plays out. A compact, gritty British gangster thriller featuring electrifying performances from Winstone and Kingsley, who won an Oscar for his explosive, nerve-shredding turn as Teddy Bass, set against the incongruously sunny backdrop of the Costa del Sol, this is a cinematic treat on the big screen.
Warnings: Nudity, Scenes of violence, Strong language/swearing

Title: Queen at Sea
Description: When Amanda (Binoche) walks in on her elderly parents in the throes of what appears to be a consensual sexual encounter her instinct is to call the police, believing her mother Leslie (Calder-Marshall) who is suffering from dementia, incapable of giving consent to husband Martin (Courtenay). As this complex, emotionally devastating and utterly gripping scenario plays out we are asked to question our preconceptions, ideas and treatment of the elderly in this devastating and superbly acted film, winner of a Silver Bear at the Berlinale. This is moral maze filmmaking at its most nuanced and sophisticated.

Title: COMA
Description: COMA is an immersive audio experience in complete darkness. You’re lying on a bunk bed inside a shipping container. Headphones on, lights out. 360-degree sound invites you to take part in a collective experiment: slip into a shared dream on the edge of consciousness. The most surrender-driven of the DARKFIELD shows, and the one that asks you to let go completely. Please remember when you leave to take your body with you.
Warnings:
Contains distressing or potentially triggering themes, More information
Takes place in complete darkness. If you are claustrophobic, suffer from PTSD/hallucinations or are scared of the dark, this show may not suit you. COMA contains themes of loss of bodily autonomy, medical procedures, comas and death.

Title: Bigger – France Showcase
Description: On stage, dancer and choreographer Sofiane Chalal brings an unconventional body that defies the codes of dance. The piece addresses deeply personal, and therefore universal, themes: the body as both ally and adversary, and the paradox – at times empowering, at times painful – between how we perceive ourselves and how others see us. Sofiane Chalal approaches these questions with great sensitivity and a distinctive physical language combining the power of hip hop with the fragility of mime. Duration : 50 minutes : 35 min performance + 15 min conversation with the artist.

Title: Sacred Creatures
Description: Three estranged siblings reunite at a rural retreat in Italy after the middle sister has been released from psychiatric treatment following a breakdown, one she experienced as a deep spiritual awakening. Frieda Luk’s artfully composed and highly compelling debut feature is a deftly woven, unpredictable and black-humoured thriller of superstition, idolatry and communal faith with a distinctive magical realist edge.

Title: The Mysterious Seelie Wight Women
Description: 16th-century Scottish Folk belief and history interwoven to tell the tale of Maggie and Jonet's initiation into the ways of the seelie wight witches. A story of faith in faerie law, friendship and nature, with some music and ritual. Two working-class Lowland Scottish women learn to make folk belief their mode of survival and a way to navigate the seismic and often dangerous changes to politics, faith and ordinary life in the century that saw the Reformation and the Scottish Witchcraft Act.
Warnings: Audience participation, Contains distressing or potentially triggering themes
Venue: Museum of Magic, Fortune-Telling and Witchcraft

Title: Forge
Description: Multi-instrumentalist Tom Oakes returns with Forge, a new work building on the award-nominated The Hearth. Traditional music is set against live composition and improvisation, threaded with archive broadcast and new writing by Kolbrún Björt Sigfúsdóttir. Stories of resistance surface in sound and speech, carried in music that changes from night to night. The Hearth was nominated for Best New Work at the MG ALBA Scots Trad Music Awards and premiered at the Edinburgh Fringe before appearing at major festivals including Celtic Connections in Glasgow.

Description: Join Jane on a search for her missing uncle, leading her to The Boline Inn and its strange, captivating women. Beneath her calm exterior, tensions simmer. Will the women bring her to boiling point? With its quirky humour, eerie atmosphere and unforgettable aesthetic, The Boline Inn – an award nominated production – 'has the ornaments of a cult classic' (AYoungishPerspective.co.uk). From Liverpool’s all-female company Meadow Report, this Edinburgh Fringe debut is a bold, uncanny exploration of community, mystery and female friendships.

Title: Autistic Musical Comedian Paul Dennis
Description: "Make the title self-explanatory", they said. Yeah. You can't say that to an autistic person and expect them not to hemorrhage. The show is funny songs and stories about office friendships, overrated lyrics, the shadowy underworld of karaoke and musical comedy itself in a choreographed maelstrom of neurodiversity. It's self-explanatory but with nothing left to the imagination, it's useless as a selling point. There; title explained. Well... sort of. Just see it, mun. You could win a crème egg.
Warnings:

Title: Boys Don't Dance
Description: Boys Don't Dance is a poignant dance theatre show by acclaimed disabled artist Marc Brew, reflecting on his lifelong journey defying societal expectations to embrace his love for dance. Combining movement with BMX and wheels, storytelling, lighting and an uplifting 80s soundtrack – alongside visual projections and animation, creating an immersive experience for audiences. Boys Don't Dance celebrates individuality and the liberating power of dance, encouraging audiences to embrace their unique passions and find strength in their differences. Commissioned by Imaginate and Aberdeen Performing Arts, supported by OneRen. MadeInScotlandShowcase.com. Longlisted: The List Festival Awards 2026 Best Kids.

Strobe lighting, More information
Haze, flickering lights, flashing lights, loud and sudden noises, BMX and wheelchair tricks and jumps at close proximity.

Description: Love science? Love comedy? Want to laugh and feel smart? Come to Stand-Up Science, a collective of fantastic scientific comedians from across the Fringe. Returning for a fifth year following successful runs in 2022 to 2025, this show will make you laugh and learn. 'Genuinely laugh-out-loud funny, genuinely interesting, genuinely original' (DailyInfo.co.uk). Each show will have a line-up of excellent science-themed comedy. From biochemistry to physics, chemistry to medicine – lots will be covered in this month's syllabus. Hosted by Matt Hobs, 'belly laughs' (BroadwayBaby.com), and featuring Alex Farrow, 'perfect' (Scotsman), and many more.

Description: Grandpa Heimer has loved the ocean since childhood. Together with grandchild Charlie, they transform everyday objects into grand maritime adventures. But as Heimer's dementia progresses, his mind drifts further out to sea, and the 'storms' grow wilder. Can Charlie find a way to steer them safely through the waves? Inspired by a true story, Roarrr Theatre blends puppetry, object theatre, and original music into a heart-warming family voyage that gently explores memory, love, and the circle of life.

Title: Carys Should be the UK’s Next Eurovision Entry
Description: Carys is campaigning to become the UK’s next Eurovision entry. In this one-woman musical comedy, she builds her case through bold vocals, unshakable self-belief and a growing list of signatures on her petition. Part manifesto, part love letter to Eurovision, the show celebrates big dreams and the reckless optimism required to think that this is going to get the BBC’s attention. Aside from sparking a panic that spirals out of their control, it forces them to question what might actually be terrorizing their under-resourced and already superstitious community. Created by the acclaimed Kook Ensemble, Sand is a non-verbal circus theatre show that blends acrobatic skill with meticulously crafted storytelling. Through visually striking, emotionally resonant performances, the company brings the experiences of people living with dementia to life, offering audiences a deeply moving experience. A must watch!

Title: Borges and Me
Description: In the 1970s, writer and student Jay Parini (Whitehead) finds himself committed to driving blind poet Jorge Luis Borges (Gnecco) across the Scottish countryside. Over the course of an eventful journey the pair form a complex and rich bond, imbued with poetry, music and melancholy. Beautifully adapted from Parini’s memoir, this gorgeously shot and superbly acted film from director Marc Turtletaub evokes memory, time and place with remarkably vivid and clear-eyed candour. Featuring terrific supporting performances from Scottish acting legends Alan Cumming, Peter Mullan and Freya Mavor, this is literate and grown-up filmmaking of the highest order.

Title: Hamlet
Description: The King of Denmark is dead, and the Queen has married his brother. Prince Hamlet, seeing spirits and feigning madness, seeks out revenge. Famously faithful to the unabridged original text, director and actor Kenneth Branagh’s adaptation boasts a star studded cast and opulent, theatrical visuals. Exploring timeless themes of corruption, truth and madness, Hamlet proves itself as timely as ever in our modern era. A magnificent epic at just over four hours, the film has long been lauded as one of the best adaptations of Shakespeare’s greatest play.

Title: Skintown
Description: Set in 1994 Northern Ireland during the IRA ceasefire, best friends Vinny and Jonty party with friends, cut deals and make plans to escape small town life. The uncertainty and instability of the time conspire against them in Walsh’s vivid, lived-in portrait of disenfranchised youth, 90s rave culture and a turbulent period in recent Irish history. Title: BEL
Description:
Louise Lockwood’s debut theatrical documentary is a compelling, sensitive portrait of Beldina Odenyo, the Kenyan-Scottish musician, singer and songwriter, who performed under the stage name, Heir of the Cursed and worked across Scotland’s theatre and poetry communities. After her acclaimed performance at the Scottish Album of the Year Awards in 2021, Bel took her own life, leaving behind raw, intimate video diaries and a hard drive full of original songs of great beauty. This stirring and beautifully composed film documents the journey her sister and friends took to release her work posthumously, including her thoughtful reflections on mental health, racism and the diaspora experience, creating a warm, insightful and deeply moving ode to a complex, intelligent and profoundly talented young woman. – Emma Boa

By Bus and Tram



Lothian Bus routes 10, 11, 15, 15a, 16, 23, 27, 45 all serve the area of Tollcross on a regular basis.

Refer to National Rail for timetables and tickets.

Outside Black Thorn Tattoo, Books N Cup and the Post Office on Home Street



Opposite the entrance to Tollcross Fire Station



Next to The Bike Station on Lauriston Place 








Refer to Edinburgh City Council’s cycling and walking guide for more information about the routes and a detailed map of the cycle parking locations.

Venue Accessibility



Physical Access to the Cameo



Both the bar and main entrance are wheelchair accessible. However, level access to the bar is only available from the street through the Lochrin Place entrance – moving between the two areas requires a wheelchair user to enter via the street.



Physical Access in the Screening Rooms



Screens 1 and 2 are accessible to customers with limited mobility, including wheelchair users. There are four wheelchair spaces in Screen 1 and two in Screen 2.



Dedicated wheelchair spaces are available in the following locations:



Screen 1: Row M, Seats 1-2 & 20-21



Screen 2: Row A, Seats 5-6 & 10-11



Aisles in our screens are located on each side of every row:



Screen 1: aisles are located next to seats A1 – M21 or seats A20, C20, E20, G20, J20, L20.



Screen 2: aisles are located next to seats A1-C1, A15, B16, and C18.



Sofa seats are double seats with no armrest in between. These are sold as two seats and are located:



Screen 1: No sofa seats



Screen 2: B1+2, B3+4, B13+14, B15+16, C1+2, C3+4, C15+16, C17+18



All seats have immovable armrests, and chairs are fixed together.



The distance of the aisles between seats – from the front of one row of seats to the back of another – is approximately 50cm. The seat base and back are approx 48cm wide; 69cm wide including armrests.



The sofa seats base and back are approximately 110cm wide; 133cm wide including armrests. These are sold as two separate seats.



Audio



All three screens are fitted with the Williams Sound hearing assistance headset system; please notify a member of staff if you wish to use a headset or induction loop compatible with a hearing aid.



Toilets



There is a fully accessible separate toilet for wheelchair users opposite the doors to Screen 1. There is an emergency call-point (the red hanging cord) inside should you need to call for assistance.



Assistance dogs



Assistance dogs are welcome at The Cameo Picturehouse. If you wish to take a dog into a performance, please let us know once you have booked your tickets, so we can ensure an aisle seat is reserved for you.



The Meadows is very close by for the exercise of assistance dogs. 



The bar is dog friendly and staff can provide water bowls and treats if the dogs are allowed.







Further Information



Cameo Picturehouse contact details



By Phone: Picturehouse’s dedicated accessibility line 02072 947908 (Text Relay call 18001 02072 947908).



By Email: Use the email form on Picturehouse’s website here.

Title: The First Annual Inaugural Grief Awards
Description: You're invited to The First Annual Inaugural Grief Awards! After losing his father to pancreatic cancer in 2020, Andreas Tsironis grieved. He grieved pretty hard. Now, he's decided he is "totally over it" and will be hosting an award ceremony to commemorate the feat! Join the comedian for an absurd and heartfelt evening in which he honours his late father and explores how grief connects those of us it leaves in its wake. Except for Andreas. Venue Accessibility



Physical Access to Picturehouse



Access to Picturehouse is step free, with a long shallow ramp from the south to north door. 



The main entrance and Box Office are located on the ground floor, accessible via a ramped, electronically assisted entrance door from Lothian Road. 



Physical Access in Picturehouse



There is step free access to wheelchair spaces and companion seats in Screens 1, 2, 3 and 4.



All seats have armrests, 580mm between armrests, and are joined together.



If you intend to transfer from a wheelchair into a cinema seat, please let the Access Booking Service know when booking so that we can find a seat that best matches your requirements.



Screen 1



Located on the First Floor which can be accessed via a passenger lift. 



Two dedicated wheelchair spaces. There are two aisles and access is level from the passenger lift at the front of the screen.



Screens 2, 3 and 4 are half a level down from the Ground Floor, accessible via a platform lift which is located on the ground floor. 



Screen 2 



Has been upgraded to level access and no longer requires a second platform lift to access.



One dedicated wheelchair space. There is one aisle and access is level from the rear right of the screen. 



Screen 3



One dedicated wheelchair space. There is one aisle and access is slightly sloped from the rear left of the screen. 



Audio



Hearing Induction and Visual Impairment systems are available in all screens using either a neck loop or two-channel infrared stethoset. 



Screen 1 also has a single channel Hearing Induction room loop which does not require infra-red sets. You can connect by switching to the ‘T-coil’ on any row.  



Toilets



There are two accessible toilets, suitable for use with wheelchairs and for changing. 



The first is located next to the Box Office on the Ground Floor with level access between the main entrance doors and the passenger lift. 



The second is located in the corridor leading to Screens 2 and 3, accessible via the stairs or a platform lift. No keys are required to use these toilets. 



The closest changing places toilet is located at Johnnie Walker, a 6 minute walk away on Princes Street.



Assistance Dogs



Assistance dogs are welcome in this venue. 



The Meadows is a ten-minute walk away for the exercise of assistance dogs.

Title: A Murder Mystery Musical – The Detective's Demise
Description: Sell-out murder mystery comedy musical returning to the Fringe! New songs. New Twists. New Turns. Detective Ben Stone is murdered at his own birthday party, snuffed out like candles on a cake. Five suspects have means, motive and opportunity, but with the detective lying "stone" dead, Ben's protege, sleuth Penelope Puck, must take on the investigation... With showstopping songs and devilish twists, Penelope attempts to solve the jaw-dropping murder, as ever more ridiculous motives are uncovered one by one – until the killer is finally revealed... Title: Olivia Xing: Baby of Colour

As an ethnic baddie, she decided to get an IUD – cuz you know what they say – DEI is out, IUD is in. The subsequent surreal gynaecologist visits become a meditation about identity, autonomy and what it means to create as a woman, alien and stand-up comedian.

Title: Birdbath
Description: Birdbath (1965) is a renowned one-act, two-hander play by Leonard Melfi, featuring the characters Frankie Basta, an unsuccessful poet working as a late-night cafeteria cashier, and Velma Sparrow, a jittery, socially isolated waitress. The play follows an awkward, tense first interaction that moves from a 24-hour cafeteria to Frankie’s basement apartment. This off-off-Broadway psychological drama evolves around themes of loneliness, trauma, repression and the search for connection. The play functions like a slow-burn psychological thriller disguised as a simple date and engages the audience through the elements of mystery, sudden shifts in stakes and unpredictable character development.

Title: Behnam Ghazanfaripour – The Music of the Santour
Description: Iranian music, with the Santour at its heart, carries centuries of emotion, poetry and cultural identity. Through music, the player aims to create dialogue, understanding and unity in a world that needs deeper human connection. In this way, art becomes a shared language beyond borders. The voice of the Santour, an ancient Persian dulcimer played with mallets, represents not only Iranian heritage, but also a universal bridge to bring people closer together across cultures, reminding us of our shared humanity.

Title: Keeping Secrets

Based on the performer’s true-life story from 1970s Boston to today, Keeping Secrets combines acting, visuals and a magic trick or two. A riveting performance, the show explores how traumatic experiences can be transformed into positive action. Creator Jim Vetter has enchanted fans internationally as a magician, mime and actor. Preview audiences call Keeping Secrets: Amazing, riveting, raw, funny, hopeful and that it 'should be on Netflix.’

With five-star reviews from such outlets as The Public Ledger and Bracket Face, this is not to be missed.

Title: Mario Adrion: Live a Little
Description: A darkly funny show about a boy from a picturesque German town who leaves it all behind to become an international fashion model. Armed with a need for approval, Mario dives headfirst into the modelling world, navigating the chaos of pseudo professional relationships, the European runway, and sketchy modelling gigs. Along the way, Mario faces unhealthy power dynamics, constant rejection, and significant sexual abuse within the industry. The show explores themes of self-love, the need for acceptance, and grappling with sexual trauma from a male perspective. It’s a story about being hot — and sad.

Title: Banker Tailor Teacher Guy
Description: From banking to tailoring, from making lingerie for strippers to working as a film extra, and finally becoming a maths teacher who teaches sewing, this solo storytelling show follows one man’s determined leap into a creative life. Low-tech and intimate, this sharp, funny story retraces those first steps through fashion studios, film sets and underfunded classrooms. Told through real garments made along the way, it’s a fast, funny and heartfelt hour about connection, friendship and the search for meaningful work, rooted in the lived experience of going all in on creativity and discovering what truly matters.

Title: Is It Too Late Now To Say Sorry?
Description: We've all said things we wish we could un-say. Broken things we wish we could un-break. But is one word enough to fix all our regrets? Acclaimed theatre-maker Adam Lenson returns to Summerhall with a new collision of gig, storytelling and autobiographical investigation. From synagogue to school playground, from online pile-ons to family fallout, Is It Too Late Now To Say Sorry? is a funny, hopeful exploration of guilt, shame and the terrible possibility of forgiveness.

Title: Bron Lewis: Chaos
Description: Bron's life is complete, utter chaos. Three kids – an emotional tweenager, a four-year old stalker and the middle one. Just when things couldn't get any harder, she bought a puppy. A million plates in the air, even more smashed on the ground around her feet. Bron wears the battle scars of an ex high-school teacher and is still reeling from the initial shock of motherhood 12 years ago. Title: Sitting (In Silence)

Description: A play disguised as a magic show where history and illusion intertwine. Enslaved in America, Henry 'Box' Brown conjures his life and reenacts his daring 1849 escape when he shipped himself to freedom inside a wooden crate. Each illusion mirrors a chapter of his journey: love, loss, confinement, faith and defiance. Gospel-infused soundscapes and stagecraft transform the theatre into a site of both sanctuary and reckoning. As boxes appear, vanish and break apart, Henry's story becomes more than spectacle – it becomes testimony, inviting audiences to witness liberation not as legend but as lived and embodied resistance.

Title: The Bride
Description: When no-one tells us who to become, are we willing to take responsibility for choosing? A physical theatre work where movement carries memory and language reveals consciousness. This is not a memorial, but a ritual of becoming. The body on stage moves through states of mechanism, imitation, adaptation, disorientation, awareness and choice. At the final altar, Er’er completes a long-rehearsed dance, not in rage or collapse, but by stepping away. The cocoon does not break into a new identity or heroic rebirth, but into an undefined body – an open state.

Title: Sculpture and Poetry (Legacy)
Description: In a surreal world of terracotta figures bound by rigid roles, each is trapped in an unchanging destiny. Armoured warriors must stare ahead, performers must always smile, and others remain forever fixed. A defiant cavalry figure breaks these rules, to be told they are only clay, not truly alive. Inspired, others also rebel, forming a caravan journeying against the flow of time through ancient cities, marketplaces, and battlefields, each searching for meaning, freedom, and their own inner truth.

Description: An abstract dance dialogue about peace, violence, and the relationship between the self and society. This dance-work invites the audience to question their own beliefs and prejudices, and to reflect on individual responsibility within a broader social context.

Venue description: Set in the iconic former Veterinary College, Summerhall Arts' programme is packed full of exciting and challenging theatre, dance, visual art and music from across the world and Scotland. Venue accessibility: We are committed to making your visit to Summerhall an enjoyable experience and we are working to make our venue as accessible as possible. The building is B-listed and is over one hundred years old and not all of our spaces are fully accessible. Our step-free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. From here, The Royal Dick pub is situated to your right as you come in (with ramp access entry to bar behind the pub) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads you up to the left and into the building where you can access our reception, boutique, cafe and some of our venues. We have lift access to some of the first floor spaces and the basement spaces. Further information about individual spaces and shows can be obtained from the box office. Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with, please do not hesitate to ask. www.summerhallarts.co.uk/accessibility/. Wheelchair accessible toilets can be found in the Royal Dick pub and on the Ground floor by the cafe. Although there is no on-site parking at Summerhall, especially during the Fringe, paid parking spaces are available on the nearby Sciennes Road. Please be aware that parking is limited and can be quite competitive. Presented as a stripped-back variety show, Lucy's first completely solo show calls on the audience to become her missing friends, stepping into roles she cannot fill alone. As the show spirals through failed spectacle, emotional manipulation and increasingly chaotic attempts at community-building, Lucy exploits the language of cabaret to unravel ideas of narcissism, celebrity and the unhinged woman. A master of theatrical manipulation and crushing personal vulnerability, she leaves audiences needing a hug, a cry and an immediate shower.

His story inspired Harriet Beecher Stowe to create Uncle Tom in the seminal novel of the 19th Century – Uncle Tom’s Cabin. This is a story that matters today in a time when histories are being erased and challenged. It is a compelling true Canadian story of triumph over adversity.

As her daughter suffers bullying, Liane has a real-world encounter with the Manosphere that stokes her rage. Mother and daughter take up boxing. They develop a taste for violence. Title: JOSIAH
Description: Based on the autobiography of Josiah Henson. Born into slavery in Maryland, enduring 41 years of unimaginable brutality and persecution before escaping to Canada. The play dramatises his unwavering resilience, determination and faith; the indomitable spirit which led him to become a respected leader, minister and teacher. His story inspired Harriet Beecher Stowe to create Uncle Tom in the seminal novel of the 19th Century – Uncle Tom’s Cabin. This is a story that matters today in a time when histories are being erased and challenged. It is a compelling true Canadian story of triumph over adversity.

Title: Big Dog
Description: Eve lands a ghostwriting job for a major true crime podcaster. Should be easy, right? She's intelligent and doesn't care about rising through the ranks. It asks who gets to tell certain stories, who profits from them, and who ultimately bears the emotional consequences.

Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with, please do not hesitate to ask. www.summerhallarts.co.uk/accessibility/. Wheelchair accessible toilets can be found in the Royal Dick pub and on the Ground floor by the cafe. Title: LANDSFRAU
Description: When the last plane left Kabul, Afghanistan vanished from Ariana’s reach. In LANDSFRAU, the return of the Taliban and the withdrawal of the western troops in 2021 triggers an auto fictional reckoning with war, memory and responsibility. Onstage, Ariana dismantles images of Afghanistan and builds her own counter-archive: fragments of family history, imagined pasts, longing and rage. Afghan folk music collides with electronic beats; Attan meets contemporary dance. Through a feminist lens, she confronts the quiet guilt of living safely abroad. Refusing explanation or absolution, this performance becomes a personal act of political resistance.

Description: Award-winning solo show. Join US comic actor Sims Holland on her Edinburgh debut as she recounts her rollercoaster journey from the depths of addiction to the challenging – and often hilarious – road of sobriety. Speckled with poetry, dotted with dance numbers and doused in honesty, Learning to Human is a heartfelt exploration of what it takes to reclaim your life. Winner: Best Autobiographical Show, United Solo, NYC 2024. Winner: Best of the Fest, Frontera Fest ATX 2024. Nominee: B Iden Payne Award, ATX 2024. 'Searing, soul bearing and completely unforgettable' (BroadwayWorld.com).

As an adult, I wondered what it would look like if I made a rom-com that actually had the lesson I needed to hear all those years ago. Then I realized: I should just tell my real story. From the director of Being Ginger (a NYTimes Critics’ Pick: 'sweet, funny, and enormously endearing') comes its live sequel. Part documentary film, part spoken-word performance, 100% real-life rom-com.

Title: Maiden | Mother | Whore
Description: An interdisciplinary mixed-media performance blending South Asian classical-contemporary dance, interactive projection, spoken word and live audience encounter. Created by Theiya Arts in collaboration with academics from Centre for Biomedicine, Self and Society at University of Edinburgh, the work explores gender, power and resistance through a transnational intersectional feminist lens. For Fringe 2026, it is presented as a theatre adaptation. A layered, intimate and politically charged space where you are invited to move through an interactive exhibition environment before entering a live performance shaped by movement, projection art and collective reflection.

Best friends Fiadh and Nolan have disappeared, hiding from the world and from the truth of what really happened. As fear tightens and outside pressure creeps closer, their bond is tested by suspicion, manipulation, and moral compromise. What begins as unwavering loyalty slowly fractures, forcing Nolan to question whether standing by the person he loves most is an act of devotion, or a dangerous refusal to see the truth.

Reality fractures as Lucy drifts between dream and nightmare, victim and liberator. Life-sized puppets and human performers collide with original music and cinematic video in an intoxicating descent into desire, fear and female emancipation. Dark, sensual and visually breathtaking, this wordless production blurs the line between beauty and horror, human and puppet, life and death.

Title: Sophia Wren: The Best Girl in the World
Description: Sophia, 'main character of the world,' remembers a teenagehood spent fantasizing about injuries that would earn her the attention she craved. Now an adult trapped inside her own damsel-in-distress mythology, her life veers into absurdity when a hurricane in New York City leaves her mysteriously pregnant. Thirteen years later, Sophia faces another adolescence unfolding against a world set ablaze by powerful men and collapsing ideals. A love letter to the Best Girl in the World and an elegy for lost childhood, this story unfolds through Sophia's dark, lyrical, hilariously filthy stand-up comedy.

Title: Diary of a Mad Man
Description: Diary of a Mad Man is a darkly comic one-man drama tracing the psychological collapse of a corporate worker whose status craving mutates into obsession. Adapted from Nikolai Gogol and relocated to contemporary Ireland, the play immerses us inside a mind where professional failure breeds paranoia, rage and terrifying logic. Consumed by race, hierarchy and fixation on his CEO’s daughter, his inner voice grows seductive, persuasive and lethal. As reality fractures, the audience becomes trapped inside his reasoning, forced to confront how ambition corrodes identity and madness feels disturbingly justified, dark, funny and deeply unsettling.

Title: A Pub Quiz for D**kheads
Description: A strictly 18+ pub quiz for know-it-alls, written and hosted by comedians. Gather your most insufferable friends, bring a charged smartphone in case you want to cheat, and grab a pint to enjoy the most ludicrous quiz of your life. Unlike millennials, we don't have mental health issues; we have a personality. We don't ghost, we divorce. And we've found our life purpose, thanks – it's a burnout with benefits. Start your day with a healthy dose of comedy. Because turmeric can only do so much. A show for those young at heart, just not in the face. Description: JFK'S been shot and Colm and Peggy want a day off school. Sure, they got one when the Pope died? Follow two best friends as they stage a protest to honour the slain U.S president. Title: Improbotics Presents: Artificial Reality
Description: Improvised show where audiences become producers of a reality show. With questionable methods, AI, wild characters and deep fake celebrities, we sabotage reality TV. Led by an executive producer, the crowd controls the show while contestants compete for audience love. Because of budget cuts, "celebrities" are recreated using our own questionable artificial reality methods (deep fakes, video generation and AR glasses to send lines from a chatbot to control the "celebrity"). As contestants get replaced by AI, the show becomes a fast-paced high-tech satire of AI slop and voyeurism, by the award-winning pioneers of robot theatre.

Framed as a school day with an unusually entertaining supply teacher, this mischievous, fast-paced journey through elements of the Key Stage 2/3 curriculums features sharp wordplay, mind-blowing trivia, visual humour and crazy antics. Mr Dali shares his own childhood poetry, rhyming balloon-modelling lesson, a joyful exploration of English language's finest Humdinger Words, and genuine improvised rhyming mind-reading to celebrate language, curiosity and confidence. The climactic show-and-tell segment provides a platform for children to share their own poetry. So, creative whippersnappers: come prepared!

The plan is simple: fix her teeth, fix her life, so that she can move up a metaphorical floor in her head and finally fix that pesky mental health. Raw, funny and disarmingly intimate, it asks the unaskable – like whether survivors should wear matching sashes – and invites audiences to laugh, reflect and heal alongside her as she rewrites her story on her terms.

Description: At a queer community event, an "inspirational" elder steps up to deliver the speech everyone expects: warm, wise and reassuring. Instead, he tells the truth. Friends are lost, old compromises resurface and survival proves messier than nostalgia allows. This is a sharp, unsentimental reckoning with queer history, intergenerational memory and what it really means to live long enough to watch your identity become marketable.

Venue accessibility: We are committed to making your visit to Summerhall an enjoyable experience and we are working to make our venue as accessible as possible. The building is B-listed and is over one hundred years old and not all of our spaces are fully accessible. If coming into Summerhall using the main entrance, please be aware that there are nine steps up to reception and the steps do not have a handrail. Our step-free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. From here, The Royal Dick pub is situated to your right as you come in (with ramp access entry to bar behind the pub) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads you up to the left and into the building where you can access our reception, boutique, cafe and some of our venues. We have lift access to some of the first floor spaces and the basement spaces. Further information about individual spaces and shows can be obtained from the box office. If you would like more information about the accessibility of particular shows, please contact us by phone on 0131 560 6243 or by email on boxoffice@summerhallarts.co.uk. Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with, please do not hesitate to ask. www.summerhallarts.co.uk/accessibility/. Wheelchair accessible toilets can be found in the Royal Dick pub and on the Ground floor by the cafe. Although there is no on-site parking at Summerhall, especially during the Fringe, paid parking spaces are available on the nearby Sciennes Road. Please be aware that parking is limited and can be quite competitive. Title: The Tin Drum
Description: A digital screening of Kazakhstan’s ART Theatre’s reimagining of Günter Grass’s landmark novel. Oskar Matzerath grows up amid the rise of National Socialism, observing the world around him with a merciless, sarcastic and perceptive gaze. His constant companion is a tin drum, through which he expresses his response to a society becoming increasingly indifferent to growing evil. Director Anton Bolkunov replaces large sections of text with a musical score, extreme vocals, movement and visual theatre, creating a distinctive theatrical interpretation in which visual, performative and musical elements become the driving force of the production.

When Sam champions a radical new production, Liz's fury erupts, not from having seen it, but from the sheer possibility of their disagreement. As their civilized world shatters in a storm of jargon and betrayal, the unthinkable happens, as furious voices of Greek tragedy and Shakespeare's figures erupt onto the stage, violently invading and transfiguring their reality. Title: I Don't Care
Description: A contemporary dance performance exploring the subtle process of shedding imposed identities and social expectations. It examines how professional roles and societal norms shape, even constrain, the body. On stage, garments such as stiff-collared shirts, structured workwear and cinched dresses become visible markers of internalized discipline and expectation. Through shared movement and interaction, I Don’t Care traces a journey: from unconscious endurance, to the awakening of discomfort, to collaborative acts of removal and finally to the emergence of the self as the symbolic layers are stripped away, to reveal the long hidden authentic selves.

Internationally recognised with the Special Award for Stage Innovation at ART-ORDO 2023, Kulager makes its UK debut through Qazaq Seasons.

Description: A new musical telling the remarkable true story of the first eight female pilots to fly for the Air Transport Auxiliary during WWII. Venue accessibility: We are committed to making your visit to Summerhall an enjoyable experience and we are working to make our venue as accessible as possible. The building is B-listed and is over one hundred years old and not all of our spaces are fully accessible. If coming into Summerhall using the main entrance, please be aware that there are nine steps up to reception and the steps do not have a handrail. Our step-free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. From here, The Royal Dick pub is situated to your right as you come in (with ramp access entry to bar behind the pub) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads you up to the left and into the building where you can access our reception, boutique, cafe and some of our venues. We have lift access to some of the first floor spaces and the basement spaces. Further information about individual spaces and shows can be obtained from the box office. If you would like more information about the accessibility of particular shows, please contact us by phone on 0131 560 6243 or by email on boxoffice@summerhallarts.co.uk. Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with, please do not hesitate to ask. www.summerhallarts.co.uk/accessibility/. Wheelchair accessible toilets can be found in the Royal Dick pub and on the Ground floor by the cafe. Although there is no on-site parking at Summerhall, especially during the Fringe, paid parking spaces are available on the nearby Sciennes Road. Please be aware that parking is limited and can be quite competitive. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Description: Comedy Against Humanity (321... on Fire!) is a high-energy, audience-interactive improv experience where the crowd drives the chaos and no two shows are the same. The self-proclaimed Auntie Hero is back, parentless and jobless to boot – and she's wondering if AI or the algorithm can predict how the crisp is going to crumble. Description: Amna is a good Muslim daughter. Mostly. At home she’s modest, obedient, invisible. Online she’s PersianBaby – bold, flirtatious, watched. Pink Rabbit is a fierce, coming-of-age, darkly funny solo play about faith, female desire and the intoxicating power of attention. As Amna hides her OnlyFans from her strict mother, the lies start to fracture. Caught between mosque and male gaze, shame and thrill, she begins to ask: who is she performing for? Raw, intimate and electric, it explores intergenerational and cultural conflict – and the dangerous moment when being seen feels better than being honest. Winner: Shedload-of-Future-Fund 2026

Title: I'm Mom
Description: When he was 18, Nate's mother died of breast cancer (he swears this show is funny). She was a beloved Chicago therapist; brilliant, generous, artistic and magic wizard lady. There was almost nothing she couldn't do. Except one thing: she never told anyone she was dying, no one got to grieve with her, no one got to say goodbye. Years later, Nate's therapist suggested Gestalt Therapy's empty chair technique: speak to the dead, then respond as them. Nate said, Absolutely Not. Years later, acting now gives him the tools to step into his mom's voice and unspoken wounds.

Together, they are Awkward and Depressed: two lost souls, searching for meaning in this bleak existence and each displaying an uncanny ability to find the humour – as well as the bizarre – in this insane world.

Title: Ali Brice: This Is The Way We Brush Our Teeth
Description: I like smiling. But only when I'm unaware of it. If you know you're smiling, you're doing it wrong. Unless you're looking at a camera. Or a dentist. I hope this show makes you smile without realising it. That would make me smile. It'll be chaotic, heartfelt and silly.  'Comic genius' **** (Skinny). 'Ali Brice is funny' **** (List). 'The most entertaining experience I enjoyed at the Fringe' (EdFringeReview.com). 'A show like no other' (Chortle.co.uk). 'A clever, off-beat talent with a penchant for risk-taking on stage' (BeyondTheJoke.co.uk).
Venue description: Hoots @ Potterrow
Venue accessibility: No wheelchair accessible toilet

Title: This Is Your Trial: UNLEASHED! The Late-Night Improvised Comedy Courtroom
Description: The strictly 18+ late-night and uncensored version of the award-winning five-star improvised comedy courtroom! You submit accusations against friends, and comedians take on the roles of judge and defence lawyers, hearing testimony, cross-examining witnesses and improvising their arguments for each case. It’s up to the audience as jury, pint in hand, to deliver their verdict. A great way to end your day at the festival!

Venue description: The Wee Red Bar is a highly popular, intimate student bar and late-night music venue located inside the grounds of the Edinburgh College of Art. Operating since the 1980s, this 210-capacity space is a staple of Edinburgh's underground music scene. It functions as a versatile venue hosting live gigs, diverse club nights, art exhibitions, and film screenings.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Michael Shafar: Inappropriate
Description: 2025 Leicester Comedy Festival Best Show Nominee. Edgy. Dark. Hilarious. In his trademark unfiltered and unapologetic style, Australian comedian, Michael Shafar, weighs into the topics that most comedians are smart enough to avoid. 'Shafar has a disarmingly relaxed approach... with a wildly inventive, darkly comic imagination.' ***** (TheEdinburghReporter.co.uk). 'He circumnavigates the line between edgy and offensive with beautiful finesse' ****½ (Age). 'If you fear comedy has gotten too politically correct, Shafar will put those fears to rest' **** (Time Out). 'He drives across taboos... this is equal opportunity Sacred Cow slaughter' (Scotsman).

Venue description: Situated in the Grassmarket, the heart of historic Old Edinburgh, and serving food and drink all day long, The Beehive Inn comprises a main bar on the ground floor and a comfortable and relaxing restaurant and bar on the first floor. Title: Spin Cycle
Description: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind meets The L Word in this bittersweet, absurdist launderette meet-cute. Eyes lock. Hearts thump. Palms sweat. But something is off. Secrets of the past are whispered, hidden under the thrum of the washing machines – can what's forgotten be remembered? This OffWestEnd Award-nominated five-star Irish play examines the space between loving someone and not, forgetting and remembering, dirty and clean clothes. A seriously refreshing show on queer love, whirring memory and finding the truth in it all. ***** (AYoungishPerspective.co.uk). Part of the 2026 Culture Ireland Edinburgh Showcase.
Warnings: Contains distressing or potentially triggering themes, Strong language/swearing

Title: Our Other Organ
Description: With brutality and humour, Boaz Barkan digs into a living body to uncover a new organ – the place where our racism resides. Our Other Organ dissects antisemitism and its impact on Jewish identity, culminating in the creation of a new Zionist body and structures of violence and domination. The performance explores the anatomy of victims and oppressors as simultaneous conditions within the same body. Moving through bodies and time, it connects personal histories to collective trauma, tracing how oppression is embodied, reproduced and transformed into systems of power, fear and ultimately, genocide.
Warnings:
Contains distressing or potentially triggering themes, More information
Descriptions of war, murder, and genocide
Venue description: Set in the iconic former Veterinary College, Summerhall Arts' programme is packed full of exciting and challenging theatre, dance, visual art and music from across the world and Scotland. Title: KINDER
Description: Winner, Best LGBTQIA+ Edinburgh Fringe Award (List). An unexpected call from a library derails a performance planned by newly arrived drag artist Goody Prostate, booked to headline the local reading hour. But as they race against the clock to scramble together a new act in real time, they spiral into a chaotic interrogation of childhood, memory and a long overdue examination of what it means to grow up. The library is open – sit down, be quiet and listen. Because sometimes, reading is what? Fundamentalist. ***** (List, BingeFringe.com, TheatreWeekly.com, AYoungishPerspective.co.uk, WhatsTheShow.com.au, SeeDoEatReview.com).

Description: Take the "fun" out of "funeral" and throw the rest away! Zoe W is holding a funeral for her childhood dog, and you're invited! Yay! Dressed in Victorian mourning garb and ready to cry on command, she'll teach you how to properly perform your grief. All she wants is your sympathy, your tears and a goddamn glass of wine (please). Sadness is Zoe's passion and this dog was Zoe's best friend. It's gonna be a rough one, so join the solemn ceremony and pay your respects with the good boys (may they rest in peace).

Description: After travelling to the UK, New Zealand, the Middle East and Indonesia. Jarryd Goundrey is back as Australia's Least Decorated Soldier. Jarryd Goundrey. Growing up in Essex, Sorabh always felt everyone around him decided who he was before he did. Wondering whether he is British or Indian enough? Should he be a lawyer or a tech bro? Title: Lewis Garnham: Work in Progress
Description: A brand new work in progress hour by one of Australia's most exciting and distinctive comedians. 'A rich source of edgy jokes' **** (Chortle.co.uk). 'A very assured, natural raconteur' **** (Scotsman). 'Relatable stories and meaningful punchlines' **** (Artshub.com.au). 'The comedian other comedians go to see' (TheatreTravels.org). Description: Oops! We Lost a Nuke is a comedic play set in the 1950s, featuring four characters performed – sometimes simultaneously –  by two actors. When an unassuming pacifist abuses his position within the US government in order to hide a nuclear warhead, it becomes clear that his affair with his secretary and his wife's affair with her doctor are the least of their worries. As the government closes in, secrets come to light.

Each year, Daniel brings incredible flamenco artists to the stage for a thrilling, authentic flamenco tablao. 2026's edition will feature Daniel himself joined by sensational singers, Inma Montero and Danielo Olivera, skillful percussionist Julian Ticotico and three spectacular dancers; Gabriela Pouso, Jara Perez and Maria Insa. This exceptional ensemble unites on stage for a show-stopping, unmissable celebration of flamenco culture, music and dance. Experience the artistry and beauty of flamenco in its purest form through breathtaking footwork, fiery energy and mesmerising choreography. Venue offers tapa and drink packages!

Would things be different if her country respected the moon, or hell, the siesta? Lured by icons of the darkness (Lilith, Diogenes, Bjork), she bewilders enemies of the night (middle school teachers). She'd stage a formal revolt, but she's lost in her own room. At this point, she'd take one unbothered day on her own sweet time. Come hungry for a defiantly disordered debut hour (on the dot).

Description: Just before Fringe 2024, Linus Karp (Diana: The Untold and Untrue Story, Gwyneth Goes Skiing, The Fit Prince) was the victim of a homophobic attack. The case never went to trial... Title: Chinese AF
Description:
Chinese AF is Kate Hu’s debut solo at the Edinburgh Fringe: fast, sharp, and proudly unfiltered. 
Born and raised in China, Kate is caught between cultures and constantly asked to “explain herself”—by her parents, society, and especially strangers online. She covers Chinese upbringing, culture shock, career choices that worry your mother, trolls with too much free time, and what happens when you date outside the algorithm, and everyone has an opinion anyway. 
She’s the first full-time comedian in her very Chinese AF family… which is why her parents still tell people she works in finance.

Title: Paws, Claws and Cobblestones
Description: Meet cheeky monkeys up to mischief on the Royal Mile, elephants on parade at the Castle and determined dogs whose loyalty made them famous. These fascinating tales, inspired by Edinburgh’s rich past, bring to life some of the city’s most unusual and beloved animal characters. Along the way, children and adults alike will be invited to sing, clap, chant, and join in the storytelling as the adventures unfold.    Perfect for families, this interactive show combines history, folklore, storytelling and song in a celebration of Edinburgh’s famous furry friends. Come along, join the fun and discover the animal antics hidden within the streets and stories of Scotland’s capital city!
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, 43-45 High Street, Edinburgh

Title: Edinburgh's Hogmanay Street Party
Description:
The world-famous Edinburgh’s Hogmanay Street Party returns to the historic city centre, to once again light-up the Edinburgh skies, at one of the world’s greatest New Year celebrations. Set against the stunning backdrop of the Edinburgh Castle, this year 45,000 revellers from around the globe, will party their way into 2027 with a feast of entertainment throughout the city centre!  

Featuring live music, DJ’s, Giant Screens, International Street Theatre, Pipers, Drummers, funfair attractions, delicious street food & drink and the return of pyrotechnic wizards Titanium designing one of the world’s best New Year firework displays.
Venue description:
Standing on street viewing are on Princes Street, with artists streamed onto the street through a series of screens. 

This is an outdoor festival event so please dress for the weather.

This is a busy, all-standing event so please prepare for crowds and arrange a meeting place with friends.

There are three main entrances to the event: Princes Street west end, Princes Street east end, and Bank Street.

Title: Torchlight Procession
Description: Launching the Edinburgh Hogmanay festival and signalling the start of global New Year celebrations, the Torchlight Procession presents a carnival atmosphere, with live Street Theatre, Fire Performers, and Drummers getting everyone warmed-up, before the Massed Pipes & Drums and Vikings from Shetland’s South Mainland Up Helly Aa’ Jarl Squad (SMUHA) lead the procession through the capital’s historic Old Town.

Title: Easy Sundays: Bear with Me
Description: From gifting bears and bearing gifts to Kings, join our young hero Beloved and his Bear on an epic journey and explore our relationship to our feral forefathers. Drawing on Icelandic saga and Scandinavian folktales join storyteller Jan Bee Brown and musician Toby Hawks for some grrreat tales. Family-friendly and dementia-inclusive.    ~~~~~    Join us in the school holidays and throughout the Scottish International Storytelling Festival 2026 for a selection of storytelling performances and events for all the family. This year’s festival explores the rich relationship between storytelling and the natural world through our theme Bird and Beast. Alongside a vibrant programme at the Scottish Storytelling Centre in Edinburgh, storytellers across Scotland bring these tales to life this autumn through the Go Local programme. We proudly celebrate Scotland’s cèilidh tradition with an invitation into the story circle, extending a warm welcome to international guests who share their stories, traditions and contemporary practices alongside Scotland’s own world-class talent. Join us for some unforgettable tales and moments that bring us closer to nature, as we follow the trail of footprints and feathers and let our imagination take flight.

Title: Samhuinn Celebration with Morvern Graham
Description: Join storyteller, illustrator, and printmaker Morvern Graham against the backdrop of her Folkloria! exhibition for a wonderful morning of stories, crafting and mask-making to celebrate Samhuinn. Come in the Halloween spirit and be prepared to get crafty before parading your new masks around the Storytelling Centre and out into Edinburgh’s Old Town. Costumes are welcomed and encouraged!
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, 43-45 High Street, Edinburgh

Title: HOGMANAY IN THE GARDENS with UNDERWORLD
Description:
Edinburgh’s Hogmanay are thrilled to welcome UK dance legends Underworld as headliners of Hogmanay in the Gardens 2026.

Making their Edinburgh Hogmanay debut, Underworld’s only Scottish performance of 2026 will include a special performance of their iconic dance anthem ‘Born Slippy (Nuxx)’ - a song ingrained in Scottish culture since featuring in Danny Boyle’s seminal film ‘Trainspotting’ in 1996. Their Hogmanay performance will follow a series of rave-reviewed shows earlier this year which celebrated the 30th anniversary of the legendary track. 

For the first time ever in the event’s history, the world-renowned Midnight Moment will be soundtracked live by Underworld on the Main Stage in West Princes Street Gardens, creating an unforgettable light, projection and firework extravaganza set below Edinburgh Castle as Scotland rings in 2027 with the ultimate dance soundtrack at one of the world’s biggest New Year celebrations. Plus very special guests to be announced. 

"We've celebrated New Years all around the world. But Hogmanay with the Scots is always EXCEPTIONAL. We only hope we can give some of that special back to the Scottish people and celebrate the only way we know how. Edinburgh, Let's Dance." - Rick Smith and Karl Hyde of Underworld
Venue description:
Standing viewing area in the Gardens (hard-standing) in front of the stage, with access to bars, food, and toilet facilities.

This is an outdoor festival event so please dress for the weather.

Title: The Last People on Earth
Description: Step into a story carved into Scotland’s landscape and carried through centuries of memory. The Last People on Earth invites you on a powerful journey back almost 2,000 years, to a defining moment in Scotland’s history: the battle of Mons Graupius.    A new show by celebrated Scottish storyteller Andy Cannon, who with his trademark warmth and wit breathes life into this ancient encounter between the Caledonians and the unstoppable force of the Roman Empire. The Last People on Earth blends storytelling, original music and the latest archaeological insights to unearth glimpses of truth buried deep in time.    What really happened on that distant day? How did this moment shape the story of a nation? Whose voices have endured — and whose have been lost?
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, 43-45 High Street, Edinburgh

Title: Exhibition: Rain
Description: When people think of Scotland, they often think of rain. Scots, in turn, have always had a lot to say about it! Our relationship with rain is both practical and deeply woven into our culture, landscape and national identity. This exhibition makes a splash as we dive into Scotland's relationship with rain. From weather forecasting, fashion, and film, to rain-soaked love stories, climate emergencies, and everything in between.

Description: Encounter birds, beasts and beasties of all kinds with a full day of free fun at the National Museum of Scotland, featuring stories and crafts for all the family.    Over the course of the day you can...Venture into the woods with Claire McNicol for stories of woodland and forest, the changing seasons and birds and beasts that live among the trees.Dive under the sea with Janis Mackay for stories of sea creatures both real and mythical and tales of tide, weather and wave.Go wild with Macastory on a Story Safari around the museum and see what you can discover.Meet the wee-est of the Wee Folk with Gauri Raje and Patrick Chadwick, featuring magical footage of the bugs and beasties who have lived here since before the Highland Boundary Fault formed (MILLIONS of years!). Title: Sruth nan Gàidheal: The Carrying Stream of Gaelic Nova Scotia
Description: Join Màiri Britton on a virtual visiting tour of Nova Scotian Gaelic tradition-bearers. For eight years, Màiri and colleagues have worked on the Cainnt is Ceathramhan/Language in Lyrics project, creating an index of 7,000 Gaelic songs and re- cataloguing and transcribing the remarkable Cape Breton Gaelic Folklore Collection. Through performance and guided listening, Màiri will share some of her favourite songs and stories from the collections. Followed by a song-circle led by Brian Ó hEadhra from the North Atlantic Song Convention (NASC).
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, 43-45 High Street, Edinburgh

Title: Deaf Storytelling in Scotland
Description: Led by BSL Storytelling Coordinator Tania Allan, this event welcomes Deaf History Scotland to share insights into its archive and the Seed Corn project, which uses tangible historical objects to inspire Deaf people to share their memories and experiences through storytelling. This in turn helps to preserve and celebrate Scotland’s Deaf history, heritage and culture.    With English interpretation from Sula Brookes.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, 43-45 High Street, Edinburgh
