Description: (Sat 24 Oct: 11am)    If you could have your own wings to take you anywhere, what would they be like?    Join Turkish storyteller, children's author and educator Nazife Burcu Takıl for a joyful, highly interactive family storytelling experience inspired by the colours, songs and traditions that connect us across cultures.    Together, you'll create your own magical wings before setting off on an unforgettable adventure through the Tunnel of Rhymes, under the Song Tree and across the shimmering Lake of Colours. Along the way, help shape the story through movement, music, imagination and play, becoming the wind, the rain, the snow and even the changing seasons.    Blending English-language storytelling with Turkish words, songs and playful participation, Wings of Colour celebrates kindness, belonging, friendship and the joy of discovering that every colour, every voice and every culture has something wonderful to share. Because when we fly together, our differences become our greatest strength.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, 43-45 High Street, Edinburgh

Title: Gira - Songs for the Orishas
Description: Brazilian artists Giulia Drummond and Mario Caribé present a ritualistic performance of music and stories of the Orishas, Yoruba deities who personify the forces of nature and timeless human archetypes. The cult of the Orishas was brought to Brazil by the enslaved Yoruba people and it endured all the oppression and violence of slavery. These spiritual traditions are filled with joy and music: chanting, drumming, dancing. It’s the music that conducts each stage of a ritual. And so this performance is designed with a ritualistic structure, following a traditional xirê - sequence in which the Orishas are saluted, sung and danced in the Gira.    ~~~~~    This year’s Festival explores the rich relationship between storytelling and the natural world through our theme Bird and Beast. Title: Under Your Skin: An Embodied Approach to Scary Stories
Description: A playful, sensory, movement- based workshop co-led by storyteller Inés Álvarez Villa and Deaf BSL storyteller Tania Allan. Drawing on Inés’s embodied storytelling practice and teaching, and her six editions at the Edinburgh Horror Festival, alongside Tania’s visual storytelling techniques and the tradition of ghost storytelling within Deaf culture, the workshop explores how suspense and dread are built through silence, gesture, and atmosphere as much as through words.    Using props, vibration and sensory experiences, Deaf and hearing participants alike will explore how embodied storytelling builds confidence, creativity and connection while bringing spooky tales to life. BSL and English interpretation will be provided throughout.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, 43-45 High Street, Edinburgh

This session, facilitated by children's author Justin Davies, is designed to delight a wide audience - perfect for families to enjoy together. Discover more than 20 myths from Ireland, Scotland, and Brittany, from epic heroes to magical mysteries.

Choosing to see your story with different eyes can help you find the depth that is hidden in plain sight. Suitable for all levels of storytellers, but please bring a story you know to work with. Title: Feathers & Fur: A Fabled Fandango
Description: Feathers & Fur: A Fabled Fandango is a tail-wagging, wing-flapping celebration of some of history’s most extraordinary animal heroes. Join storytellers Lea Taylor and Nicola Wright for a lively mix of traditional storytelling, song, humour and audience participation as they uncover the remarkable true tales of courageous dogs and heroic pigeons.    Meet Laika, the space-travelling dog who reached for the stars, Winkie the pigeon whose actions helped save lives during wartime, and other feathered and furry legends whose bravery, loyalty and determination have often gone unnoticed. Along the way, discover why pigeons may be far cleverer than their reputation suggests, and whether dogs really deserve the title of “man’s best friend”.    You are invited to sing along, join in a playful Quiz of Courage, and compete for the chance to earn prestigious honours in the Golden Poop Scoop Awards in a heartwarming, quirky and entertaining adventure celebrating the animals who have worked, served and sometimes saved us without ever asking for the credit.

Title: An Audience with Dog and Jean (The Man Who Planted Trees)
Description: Puppet State Theatre Company’s The Man Who Planted Trees ran from 2006 to 2022 touring worldwide, clocking up over 1,800 performances telling the story of Elzéard Bouffier and his famously loquacious dog, Dog. Now, to mark the show’s 20th anniversary, Richard Medrington and Rick Conte return to their favourite venue, alongside Puppet State’s Elspeth Murray. Expect reminiscences, audience questions, favourite bits, and touring stories. Pssst - he’s still in the basket!
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, 43-45 High Street, Edinburgh

Title: Psyche and Eros - Exploring the Story

Dawne McFarlane will lead gentle movement, telling and drawing exercises that you can continue creating with, whilst musicians Maryem Tollar and Sophia Grigoriadis invite us to expand our imagination beyond words. Explore moments of ancient wisdom and how they resonate with you now..

There will also be a rare chance to practice the Nordic cow call “kulning” with Satu Lankinen.

Title: Deiseil: Dancing in Time
Description: A powerful exploration of how stepdance, Scotland’s percussive dance, was lost… and how its revival became woven into a lifelong friendship. Experience a compelling journey across centuries of tradition told through fiddle, feet, Gaelic song and story, in an immersive performance which draws you in to the heart of our heritage.    Deiseil means 'ready' in Scottish Gaelic: be ready for a mesmerising reflection on how issues of culture, identity and connection still resonate through society today. Groundbreaking work from award-winning director Gerry Mulgrew, dancer Alison Carlyle and musician Amy Geddes. For this performance Amy and Alison will be joined by musicians Mairi Campbell, Fin Moore and Sarah Hoy.    A force of nature and soul, Mairi’s voice has stirred hearts across the globe. Mairi Campbell is a Scottish Traditional Music Hall of Fame inductee, with numerous national and international awards to her name. Deeply personal, politically resonant, and artistically fearless, Mairi’s work reaches into cultural memory and lived experiences. Find out more at mairicampbell.scot.    Fin Moore plays the Highland pipes, Border pipes and Scottish Small Pipes and is also a very successful pipemaker. Fin also has a reputation as a teacher of pipes, and runs exciting music retreats through Far North Retreats. He has played solo and with bands including, InB, Seudan, Dannsa, Slainte Mhath and Back of the Moon.    Sarah Hoy was born into a musical family in Edinburgh, learning fiddle from her father Derek Hoy, and later with Mairi Campbell. Sarah enjoys playing with Bella McNab’s Dance Band, her favourite place to be is playing for dancing! Sarah is now a primary teacher in the Gaelic Medium primary school in Edinburgh and enjoys teaching fiddle each week through Portobello Fun Fiddle.    ‘This is the most joyful show I’ve seen so far this Fringe.’ ★★★★★ (Scotsman)★★★★★ (AllEdinburghTheatre.com)

Join Ada on a tiny world adventure over an extraordinary hand-felted landscape as she uncovers the secret of the ravens.    Director, storyteller, performer and puppeteer Freda O'Byrne uses an eclectic mix of genres to explore the stories of ordinary people in extraordinary circumstances. Her Suitcase Stories take audiences into a magical tiny world entirely within a suitcase, reaching out and engaging their imaginations through storytelling and puppetry.

Title: Caoidh na Gaoitheig/A Resounding Voice (Alan Bruford Lecture)
Description: Tradition accrues and is transformed through relational and referential encounters, both anticipated and unanticipated, between uncertain and precarious human and more-than- human lives. Amid displacement, migration, and the loss of languages and species, Dr. Tiber Falzett (Head of Irish Folklore in the School of Irish, Celtic Studies and Folklore, University College Dublin) asks what these ways of knowing carry, and what is lost when the voices that carried them fall silent.    Presented in memory of Scottish scholar Alan Bruford in partnership with the University of Edinburgh’s Department of Celtic and Scottish Studies.

Title: National Theatre of Scotland at 20: Culture, Democracy, and the Stateless Nation
Description: As the National Theatre of Scotland and the Scottish Storytelling Centre both mark their twentieth anniversaries, this special event brings together artists, academics, cultural leaders, public figures and audiences to explore the relationship between theatre, storytelling, literature and democratic life in Scotland. The event opens with a panel discussion featuring followed by a special in-conversation event with Nicola Sturgeon and Joyce McMillan.    Session 1: Lightning Panel and Audience Discussion   A panel of invited guests will spark the discussion with 5-minute reflections on the NTS’s 20th Anniversary and Scotland’s culture and democracy today, drawing on their experiences across theatre-making, cultural scholarship, playwrighting and community participation. We will hear from Jackie Wylie (Artistic Director and Co-Chief Executive, National Theatre of Scotland), Steve Byrne (Chief Executive, TRACS Traditional Arts and Culture Scotland), Hannah Lavery (Poet, Playwright and Performer) and Dr Stephanie Lehner (Senior Lecturer, Queen's University Belfast, specialising in culture, conflict and reconciliation). The session will be chaired by Dr Paula Sledzinska (Visiting Research Fellow at IASH).    Session 2: Nicola Sturgeon in Conversation with Joyce McMillan   Bringing together insights from political leadership, cultural advocacy and critical commentary, this conversation between Nicola Sturgeon and Joyce McMillan will reflect on some of Scotland’s most influential dramatic and literary works, and the ways in which they have shaped Scotland’s civic imagination. It offers a rare opportunity to hear Scotland’s longest-serving First Minister and one of the country’s most respected cultural critics reflect together on the power of dramatic and literary culture to influence national consciousness, foster dialogue and democratic resilience, and contribute to the making of contemporary Scotland.    ~~~~~    The public programme forms part of the wider National Theatre of Scotland at 20: Culture, Democracy, and the Stateless Nation Unconference. The event, as well as the planned follow-up parliamentary session, are supported by the British Academy Early Career Researcher Network, Institute for Advanced Studies in the Humanities (IASH), University of Edinburgh, Research Institute of Irish and Scottish Studies (RIISS), University of Aberdeen, LLSETI Research Laboratory at Université Savoie Mont Blanc (Chambéry, France), Stories, Place, and Northern Communities Research Centre (SPeiR), Robert Gordon University, the Scottish Storytelling Centre and the Scottish International Storytelling Festival.

Title: The Journey of Leonardo
Description: The story of a boy, born into difficulties, who would become an artist and scientist of unending fame and influence. Considered strange by many in his small Tuscan village, he must embark on a long physical and spiritual journey to set himself free from prejudice.    A poetic and intense story- musical performance about the early years of Leonardo Da Vinci and the endless possibilities of every human when they manage to break free from a predetermined destiny. Created and performed by Paola Balbi and Davide Bardi with original live music from Mario Costanzi.    This project is made possible thanks to the support of the Italian Ministry of Culture and the Italian Institute of Culture in Edinburgh.    ~~~~~    This year’s Festival explores the rich relationship between storytelling and the natural world through our theme Bird and Beast. Alongside a vibrant programme at the Scottish Storytelling Centre in Edinburgh, storytellers across Scotland bring these tales to life this autumn through the Go Local programme. We proudly celebrate Scotland’s cèilidh tradition with an invitation into the story circle, extending a warm welcome to international guests who share their stories, traditions and contemporary practices alongside Scotland’s own world-class talent. Join us for some unforgettable tales and moments that bring us closer to nature, as we follow the trail of footprints and feathers and let our imagination take flight.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, 43-45 High Street, Edinburgh

Title: Dedalus and Icarus
Description: Bologna’s Fraternal Compagnia APS presents the myth of Dedalus and Icarus, reinterpreted in Dario Fo and Franca Rame’s distinctive ironic style as a timeless tale of rebellion and a satire of power. Gabriel Bird’s jester-like theatrical performance explores the conflict between generations, the limitations of human nature, and the desire for freedom and escape through ingenuity.    This performance is part of the Dario Fo centenary celebrations promoted by the Fondazione Fo Rame. Title: Masquerade Mask
Description: Welcome to the world of Commedia dell’Arte and the great characters of Italian theatrical tradition, including Pantalone, Il Dottore, the Captains and the Lovers. Through improvisation, pantomime, and the use of traditional masks, this performance from Bologna’s Fraternal Compagnia APS explores universal themes of love, power, poverty, and human nature, breaking down any barrier between performers and the audience. Follow the hoofprints of the horses in the Tuscan countryside and the trails of the snakes in the fresh grass of the north, where animals and imaginary beasts populate the daily lives and dreams of people. Title: Night Afore Party with The Fratellis
Description:
Making their Edinburgh’s Hogmanay debut and marking 20 years of seminal album Costello Music, The Fratellis headline a very special Night Afore Party beneath Edinburgh Castle!

One of Scotland’s most iconic live bands, The Fratellis burst onto the scene with their era-defining debut album Costello Music in September 2006, delivering anthemic hits including Chelsea Dagger, Whistle for the Choir and Henrietta. With an unmistakable energy and a feel-good live show, this is set to be an unforgettable night underneath Edinburgh Castle to kick-start 2026 Hogmanay celebrations. Plus very special guests to be announced.

"It's such an honour & privilege to be asked to perform at this year's Hogmanay celebrations in a city that we hold so close to our Hearts" - The Fratellis
Venue description:
Standing viewing area in the Gardens (hard-standing) in front of the stage, with access to bars, food, and toilet facilities.

This is an outdoor festival event so please dress for the weather.

Title: Artistic Translation for Performance Storytelling
Description: A unique opportunity for storytellers and interpreters who wish to make their stories more engaging and accessible for audiences who speak a different language. Paola Balbi and Davide Bardi share their developed method and experience with live story translation in different languages, gathered from 20 years of international experience at festivals around the world. This method can be applied to any language (including sign language) and can provide effective artistic translation for any story performance.    Please note, participants should be able to communicate in at least one other language besides English.    This project is made possible thanks to the support of the Italian Ministry of Culture and the Italian Institute of Culture in Edinburgh.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, 43-45 High Street, Edinburgh

Title: An Introduction to Commedia dell'Arte
Description: A special opportunity to learn some of the history and practice of Commedia dell’Arte with Bologna’s famous Fraternal Compagnia APS. Originating in Padua in 1545, Commedia dell’Arte is the Italian theatrical tradition which utilises body expression, improvisation, mask work, physical awareness and theatrical storytelling skills to create a relationship between performers and spectators. Explore the roots of Italian theatre and folk storytelling and discover techniques to help develop a relationship with your audience in this ancient, but fully relevant, artform.    This project is made possible thanks to a partnership with the ATER Fondazione - Regione Emilia-Romagna and support from the Italian Institute of Culture in Edinburgh.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, 43-45 High Street, Edinburgh

Title: The Great Instauration with Gayle Chong Kwan
Description: Join artist Gayle Chong Kwan on an interactive creative restorying session to explore themes in The Great Instauration (2026) her installation in the Grand Gallery of the National Museum of Scotland, as part of the 2026 Edinburgh Science Festival, that explored science as a culturally embedded process shaped by social history, power, and omission. Chong Kwan will share the storytelling at the heart of her practice and recent work, on a journey through research, art, collections and archives.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, 43-45 High Street, Edinburgh

Title: Closing Circle
Description: An open conversation and social space, to explore the networks and ideas that connect us. Led by the Scottish Storytelling Forum, this is a chance to reflect together on this year’s festival and harness energy for future ideas, projects and stories.    BSL interpretation by Emmy Kauling.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, 43-45 High Street, Edinburgh

Title: Guid Crack Storytelling Session
Description: A Bird and Beast themed festival Samhuinn special of Edinburgh’s long-running storytelling night. Join us for a open session of stories, led by host Beverley Bryant.

Title: Spun Stories and Unspun Fates
Description: Underground in a grassy knoll, three spinsters spin both flax and stories. Storytellers Freya McCall, Sháneen McGurnaghan and Nina Willms incorporate folk tales, songs and historically-inspired stories of women weaving themselves agency alongside the spiders and supernatural sisters who spin fate. Followed by a short discussion.

Title: Weather Spirits and Rain Lore
Description: Join storytellers Sandra Codd-MacDonald, Mio Shudo and Donald Smith for an afternoon of traditional tales and folklore exploring landscape, weather and nature spirits from Scotland, Japan and South America. There will also be an opportunity to visit the current exhibition Rain which looks at how rain has shaped Scottish culture, landscape and national identity.

Title: Morning Circle with Dawne McFarlane
Description: Start your festival day with a relaxed morning session of story sharing and networking. Join old friends and new ones, to shake off the dust together!    This gathering is hosted by Dawne McFarlane, who guides a conversation on storytelling inspired by her book Fairytales, Families and Forests (co-authored with Georgiana Keable).
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, 43-45 High Street, Edinburgh

Title: Animal Magic
Description: Travel to lands of myth and legend. Meet magical beasts and birds and bugs. Learn about wondrous creatures of our own world. Together, we’ll rediscover ways to enjoy and protect nature’s magic. Part interactive storytelling performance, part craft workshop, all fun!    Inspired by the storyteller's experience with the Jane Goodall Institute and Marine Conservation Society, Animal Magic invites young explorers and their grown-ups to (re)connect with the birds and beasts around us, retelling a classic Irish fairy tale to explore and celebrate the wonders of the natural world. Might their realness make these creatures all the more magical? Created, performed and facilitated by Kate Johnson, PhD.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, 43-45 High Street, Edinburgh
